syncHazards.description: WRITTEN: the task store, by the consumer's onDragMove invoked at L161 (SummaryBar.tsx:145 -> taskStore.batchMovePositions, which does setTasks(...)). READ: the same task store, by the consumer's onDragEnd invoked at L177 in the same synchronous stack — TaskLayer.tsx:98-102 handleResizeEnd calls buildCtx(taskId) and resolveResizeConstraints(taskId, ctx), both of which re-read task geometry out of the store. In 1.x the L161 write committed synchronously so L177 saw the final dragged position. In 2.0 the write is staged in _pendingValue and, because a DOM event handler runs with no owner (dev.js read(): the `!c` branch returns el._value), the L177 read path gets the PRE-drag geometry. Constraint resolution and any date persistence therefore run against the position the bar had before the last frame — the drag visually lands correctly but the committed dates are off by the final delta, and dependent-task constraint pushes are computed from stale coordinates.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Import flush from 'solid-js' and call it between the final onDragMove and onDragEnd: `if (pendingMove) { onDragMove?.(pendingMove, dragData, dragStateNow); pendingMove = null; flush(); }`. Better long-term: change the UseDragOptions contract so onDragEnd receives the resolved final geometry as part of DragMove/DragData instead of re-reading the store, which removes the ordering dependency entirely.

syncHazards.description: WRITTEN: dragState (L218) and isDragging (L219). READ: dragState at L130 inside handleMouseMove and L155 inside handleMouseUp — handlers that are registered at L224-225 in this very same synchronous run. In a real browser the mousedown handler returns, the JS stack empties, the microtask checkpoint runs the flush, and the next mousemove arrives as a fresh task, so the guards see the committed new value. But any code that dispatches mousedown and then mousemove/mouseup without yielding — every synthetic-event unit test (`el.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('mousedown')); document.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('mousemove'))`), and any programmatic drag driver — stays inside one task, so no microtask checkpoint occurs between the statements. handleMouseMove reads the committed 'idle', hits `dragState() === 'idle'` at L130, and returns immediately. The drag is a complete no-op with no error: pendingMove is never set, the RAF loop never starts, and onDragMove/onDragEnd never fire.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Introduce the non-reactive mirror `let dragStateNow: DragState = 'idle';` written next to each setDragState, and switch every internal guard (L79, L84, L130, L155, L161, L177, L196) to read it. The signal then exists purely for rendering. This is zero-cost and matches how the file already treats dragData/rafId/pendingMove. A flush() after L219 also works but pays a full graph flush on every mousedown.

syncHazards.description: WRITTEN: overlay, at L126 from handleMouseMove (visible: true once the 5px threshold is passed). READ: overlay at L135 in handleMouseUp, whose result drives `wasDragged` at L136 and is passed as the hit-test box to findBoxHits at L151. When mousemove and mouseup land in separate tasks (normal browser use) the flush has run and this is correct. When they are dispatched in one task — synthetic-event tests, or any driver that replays a gesture synchronously — overlay() returns the committed HIDDEN, `wasDragged` is false, and control takes the click-not-drag branch at L145: instead of selecting the boxed tasks the hook CLEARS the selection. A silent, exactly-inverted outcome.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Mirror the rect in a plain variable: `let overlayNow: BoxOverlay = HIDDEN;` assigned alongside setOverlay at L126, L137 and L179, and read `overlayNow` at L135 instead of `overlay()`. The signal stays for TaskLayer.tsx:293-301's JSX. Note the surrounding code is already correct in shape — L135 captures into `current` before the L137 write and everything downstream uses `current` — so this is a one-line read swap, not a restructure.

syncHazards.description: WRITTEN: dragState('idle') at L183 in handleMouseUp, while `dragData = null` at L185 takes effect immediately. READ: dragState at L196 in startDrag, which guards against starting a second drag. The two truths diverge for the rest of the task. Direction (a): mouseup then a programmatic/synthetic mousedown in the same task — L196 reads the stale 'dragging_bar' and refuses the new drag. Direction (b): two mousedowns in the same task (double-dispatch, or a synthetic click that fires mousedown twice) — L196 reads the stale 'idle' both times, startDrag runs twice, and document mousemove/mouseup listeners are registered twice while L180-181 only ever removes one pair, leaking a listener that keeps firing after the gesture ends. Every other guard in the file ANDs against `!dragData` and so survives; L196 is the only one that does not.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Read the `dragStateNow` mirror at L196. As a cheap standalone patch that fixes direction (a) only, add the dragData check the other guards have: `if (dragStateNow !== 'idle' || dragData) return;`.

syncHazards.description: WRITTEN: dragState (L218) and isDragging (L219). READ: whatever the consumer's onDragStart callback reads, invoked at L221 in the same synchronous run. The hook is partly protected because it threads `state` through as an explicit argument, and the current consumer (SummaryBar.tsx:105-124) only reads the x()/y() memos and taskStore.getBarPosition(), none of which depend on dragState. But the hook's public contract advertises `dragState`/`isDragging` accessors alongside a callback that fires before they are readable, so any consumer that writes `if (isDragging())` inside onDragStart silently gets false. The same trap applies to the demo consumers (GanttPerfIsolate.tsx:1180, index-test.tsx:1429/1528) which destructure dragState.

If a consumer genuinely needs the reactive value, call flush() between L219 and L221.

Gantt.tsx:485 is the only caller and it does nothing after the call, so nothing is broken today — but the hook's whole reason to exist is 'imperative handler writes an id, memos derive the view', which is precisely the shape deferred writes invalidate. The identical pattern applies to showHover at L76-80.

This is the textbook 'double functional update in one tick' shape and looks like it should collapse to only the last id. VERIFIED SAFE by reading the rc.6 runtime: dev.js line 4944 computes the updater's argument as `const currentValue = el._pendingValue === NOT_PENDING ? el._value : el._pendingValue;` — functional setters chain off the STAGED value, so each add() sees the accumulated Set. Recorded here so the migration does not 'fix' a non-bug, and to fix the boundary of the rule: only *non-functional* setter calls (and reads through the accessor) observe the committed value; updater callbacks do not.

syncHazards.description: WRITTEN: dragState, in the mousedown task (L218) and the mouseup task (L183). READ: dragState at L79/L80/L84 from inside the requestAnimationFrame callback, which runs unowned and therefore always sees committed state. Currently correct by accident: RAF fires in a later task than the mousedown, so the flush has landed. It becomes wrong under fake timers or a RAF shim that drains the queue inside the scheduling task — every drag frame would be dropped at L79 — and it is fragile if startRaf is ever moved from handleMouseMove (L148-150) into startDrag itself, which would put the first rafLoop read in the same task as the staged write on a browser that batches RAF aggressively.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Read `dragStateNow` at L79, L80 and L84. This also removes three reactive reads per animation frame from the hot drag path.

structuralConcerns: useDrag's core design — one createSignal serving both as the render source and as a synchronous imperative gate — is the single structural item in this batch. Seven internal call sites (L79, L84, L130, L155, L161, L177, L196) read `dragState()` expecting the value just written. The fix is not a rewrite of the state machine but a discipline change the file already applies to its other state: keep `dragState`/`isDragging` as signals for output only, and add `let dragStateNow: DragState = 'idle'` next to the existing `let rafId`, `let pendingMove`, `let dragData` (L73-75) as the authoritative synchronous truth. Every guard reads the mirror; every setter writes both. isDragging should simultaneously collapse into `createMemo(() => dragState() !== 'idle')`, removing a second independently-staged node. Do this before touching anything else in the file — it resolves five of the nine sync hazards at once.

useDrag's public API contract assumes synchronous propagation across the hook boundary. `onDragMove` is where consumers write the task store, `onDragEnd` fires in the same synchronous stack at L177, and the actual consumer chain (SummaryBar.tsx:148 -> TaskLayer.tsx:98 handleResizeEnd -> buildCtx -> resolveResizeConstraints) re-reads the store to resolve constraints. No amount of local rewriting inside useDrag fixes a consumer that reads back what a sibling callback wrote. Two viable designs: (1) a flush() between the final onDragMove and onDragEnd — one line, preserves the current contract, costs one full graph flush per gesture end; or (2) widen DragMove/DragData so onDragEnd receives the resolved final geometry as data and consumers never re-read the store. (2) is the better end state; (1) is the correct first migration step.

useBoxSelect has the same dual-role signal problem as useDrag but in miniature and with a much smaller blast radius: only `overlay()` at L135 is read imperatively. Worth calling out that L135-L137 is otherwise the model 2.0 pattern — capture into a local BEFORE writing, then use the local — and the rest of the drag code in this repo should be brought to that shape.

useBarConfig is a per-instance memo factory (7 memos x every Bar) and 2.0's switch to eager, non-lazy memos silently converts it from a lazy-evaluation optimization into a mount-time cost. Its own header comment says it exists to avoid repeated work. Blanket-adding `{ lazy: true }` to all seven restores 1.x semantics and adds autodisposal, but note the tradeoff the option carries (signals.d.ts MemoOptions.lazy): a lazy memo that loses all subscribers is torn down and recomputed from scratch on the next read, so for Bars that are virtualized in and out of view this can trade mount cost for churn. Measure before committing to lazy on the always-read ones (readonly, columnWidth); apply it unconditionally to the rarely-read ones (showExpectedProgress, ignoredPositions, readonlyProgress).

useBarConfig depends on ganttConfigStore.makeSetter (ganttConfigStore.ts:150-166), a Setter<T> shim over a store path that both reads `state[key]` to compute `prev` for updater-form calls AND returns `state[key]` after `setState(key, next)`. Under deferred writes the trailing `return state[key]` returns the PRE-write value, so the shim's Setter contract ('returns the new value') is broken, and consecutive updater-form calls in one tick chain off committed state rather than staged state — unlike a real signal setter, which chains correctly. This is out of this batch's file list but it is the data source behind all seven useBarConfig memos, so useBarConfig's correctness depends on that shim being fixed. It also uses the removed store path-setter form and `produce` (ganttConfigStore.ts:2, 175, 187, 197) which must migrate to `setState(draft => {...})`.

useGanttModals memos return live store proxies (taskStore.getTask returns `tasks[id]` directly, taskStore.ts:71-73) into TaskPopup/TaskModal. In 2.0 reading proxy fields inside a createEffect apply callback emits STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED. Either snapshot() at the memo boundary in this hook, or audit the two modal components for apply-phase proxy reads. Snapshotting here is the cheaper fix and is confined to four lines (L47, L52, L57, L62).

Test posture for this batch: the two gesture hooks are only reachable through synthetic DOM events, and neither has a unit test today (tests/boxSelect.test.ts covers only the pure findBoxHits helper and needs no changes). Any new test for useDrag/useBoxSelect must yield between dispatches — `await Promise.resolve()` or an explicit `flush()` after each dispatchEvent — because mousedown/mousemove/mouseup dispatched back-to-back in one task never reach a microtask checkpoint, and the guards at useDrag.ts:130 and useBoxSelect.ts:135 will read pre-gesture state. Also ensure @solidjs/vite-plugin's vitest posture keeps the 'browser' condition (test.environment must not be 'node'), or the server build resolves and there is no subscription graph at all.
audits.summary:
Four files, 663 lines, all read in full; imports traced one level into stores/selectionStore.ts, stores/taskStore.ts, stores/ganttConfigStore.ts and consumers components/SummaryBar.tsx, components/TaskLayer.tsx, components/Gantt.tsx, components/Bar.tsx.

MECHANICAL SURFACE IS NEARLY ZERO. All four files import only from 'solid-js' and only symbols that still exist in 2.0 (createSignal, createMemo, onCleanup, Accessor — verified in solid-js-2.0.0-rc.6/types/index.d.ts line 1-2). Grepping the batch for batch/on(/createComputed/produce/unwrap/mergeProps/splitProps/onMount/createEffect/createResource/classList/Index/Provider/createContext/untrack/createSelector returns nothing. No JSX in any of the four (.ts only), so no control-flow, context, ref or DOM-namespace sites. topLevelReadCount is 0 — useBarConfig reads props exclusively inside memo bodies, so no STRICT_READ warnings.

SMA REPORT — both of its entries for this batch are DISPUTED. sma-report.txt:315 (useBoxSelect.ts:189) and :319 (useDrag.ts:250) demand migrating onCleanup to a returned cleanup function. Neither needs to change: onCleanup is still exported from solid-js 2.0, both calls sit at hook top level under a component owner (not inside onSettled/createTrackedEffect, so CLEANUP_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE does not apply), and the onCleanup docstring (signals.d.ts:1-41) names library/custom-primitive internals as its remaining home. Converting to onSettled would be worse — neither hook has settle-phase setup, since both attach their document listeners lazily from a mousedown.

THE REAL WORK IS DEFERRED WRITES. Both gesture hooks use one signal for two jobs — reactive render source and synchronous imperative gate. useDrag reads dragState() at seven internal sites expecting a value it just staged (L79, L84, L130, L155, L161, L177, L196); useBoxSelect does the same once at L135. Verified in the rc.6 runtime that an unowned reader (every DOM event handler and RAF callback) takes the `!c` branch of read() and gets el._value, the committed value. Fix is a plain mirror variable next to the existing `let rafId / pendingMove / dragData`, not a redesign.

TWO HIGH-SEVERITY HAZARDS. (1) useDrag.ts:177 — the consumer's onDragMove writes the task store at L161 and the consumer's onDragEnd re-reads it at L177 in the same stack (SummaryBar.tsx:148 -> TaskLayer.tsx:98 handleResizeEnd -> buildCtx -> resolveResizeConstraints), so constraint resolution runs on pre-drag geometry; needs flush() or an API change that passes final geometry explicitly. (2) useDrag.ts:224 — document listeners are registered in the same synchronous run as the staged setDragState, so any same-task synthetic mousemove reads 'idle' at L130 and the drag is a silent no-op; this makes every synthetic-event test of the drag path fail.

ONE VERIFIED NON-BUG worth recording so it is not "fixed": useBoxSelect.ts:156's `for (const id of hits) sel.add(id)` looks like the classic double-functional-update-in-one-tick failure but is safe — dev.js:4944 computes the updater argument as `_pendingValue === NOT_PENDING ? _value : _pendingValue`, so functional setters chain off staged state. Only non-functional writes and accessor reads see committed state.

BEYOND THE SMA'S SCOPE: 12 createMemo calls (7 in useBarConfig, 5 in useGanttModals) are all legal 1-arg form but change behavior because 2.0 memos are eager and non-lazy by default. useBarConfig runs per Bar, so a chart with hundreds of bars now eagerly computes 7 memos and opens 7 store subscriptions per bar at mount — a mount-time regression on a file whose docstring says it exists for performance. Additionally useGanttModals' two barPosition memos wrap taskStore.getBarPosition, which allocates a fresh object per call, so with default reference equals they notify every frame during a drag; and its getTask memos leak live store proxies into TaskPopup/TaskModal, risking STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED in those components' effect apply phases.

47 sites, 8 sync hazards, 7 structural concerns. Effort M: mostly small local edits, but useDrag's mirror-variable refactor and the L161/L177 flush must be done together and verified against a real drag.

syncHazards.description: WRITE: any taskStore mutation that changes the key SET without changing the key COUNT in one tick — e.g. removeTask('a') (setTasks('a', undefined)) followed by updateTask('b', t) , or updateTasks(arr) replacing N tasks with a different N-length set. READ: `taskKeys.length === cachedTaskCount` at line 78 returns the stale `cachedGrouping`. Under 1.x each unbatched setter flushed render effects synchronously, so the visibleTaskIds memo re-ran between the two writes and observed the intermediate count. rc.6 stages every write in a tick and flushes once, so both writes collapse into ONE memo recompute with an unchanged count — the grouping (and therefore every rendered bar) silently keeps deleted tasks and drops added ones until an unrelated count change occurs.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Delete the count heuristic. Track the key set for real: `const tasksByResource = createMemo(() => { const t = props.taskStore?.tasks; if (!t) return new Map(); const keys = Object.keys(t); return untrack(() => buildGroups(t, keys)); });` — Object.keys on the proxy inside the tracked compute subscribes to ownKeys, so add/remove/replace all invalidate. If the O(keys) scan is too costly, have taskStore expose a monotonic `revision` signal bumped by every mutating method and cache on that.

syncHazards.description: Identical defect to useTaskVirtualization.ts:78, duplicated: `taskKeys.length === cachedTaskCount` (line 53) plus `cachedTaskCount = taskKeys.length` (line 57), consumed by the visibleTasks memo at line 80. Same-tick add+remove now coalesces into one flush and the cache never invalidates, so TaskLayerMinimal (the perf-demo path, Gantt.tsx:597) renders a stale task list.

syncHazards.description: WRITE-THEN-READ across a call boundary. Bar.tsx:300-302 does `props.taskStore?.updateBarPosition(taskId, { width: newWidth }); onDateChange?.(...); onResizeEnd?.(taskId);` inside one keydown handler. onResizeEnd is TaskLayer.tsx:98 -> resolveResizeConstraints, which at line 87 READS `ctx.taskStore.getBarPosition(taskId)` and feeds taskBar.x/taskBar.width into resolveConstraints, then WRITES cascade updates at line 99. In rc.6 the updateBarPosition write is still staged, so getBarPosition returns the PRE-resize width: successors are cascaded to positions computed from the old geometry, and because the cascade write itself lands in the same flush, the wrong positions are committed rather than corrected. Same shape on the drag path (useBarDrag.ts:271-278) whenever mouseup lands in the same tick as the final mousemove.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Stop re-reading state the caller just wrote. Widen the callback to carry geometry — `onResizeEnd(taskId, { x, width })` from Bar.tsx and useBarDrag.ts, threaded through TaskLayer.tsx:98 into resolveResizeConstraints(taskId, ctx, geom) — and use `geom` in place of the getBarPosition call at line 87. If the signature must stay, wrap the resize block in `flush(() => { ... })` at the Bar call site so the write commits before the read; that restores 1.x ordering at the cost of a synchronous cascade.

syncHazards.description: READ-then-WRITE over the same rows. constrainTaskPosition reads the dragged bar (line 60) and — inside resolveConstraints via the bound getBarPosition/getTask from buildContext (lines 40-41) — reads every successor's committed position, then writes those successors with updateBarPosition (lines 68-73). Invoked from TaskLayer.tsx:88 on every drag tick (useBarDrag.ts:155-164 and :183-196). Correct only while exactly one invocation happens per commit. rc.6 coalesces all writes in a tick, so two constrain calls in the same tick (coalesced pointer events, a keyboard repeat burst, or a batch-drag path that also calls handleClampBatchDelta at TaskLayer.tsx:146 while batchMovePositions from the previous tick is still staged) both compute cascades against the same stale base; the second overwrite wins and the intermediate delta is lost.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Do the read and the cascade write in a single store draft so reads see staged state: `setTasks(draft => { for (const succ of successors) { const bar = draft[succ]?._bar; ...compute...; if (bar) Object.assign(bar, update); } })`, returning constrainedX as the function result. Alternatively keep the current structure but make useBarDrag rAF-coalesce so at most one constrain call runs per flush.

syncHazards.description: `expandedTasks: Set<string>` lives inside a createStore and is mutated IN PLACE via `setState('expandedTasks', produce(set => set.add/delete(taskId)))` (toggleTaskExpansion line 171, expandTask line 188, collapseTask line 198). rc.6 does not proxy built-in collections, so an in-place Set mutation notifies nothing at all. Consumer: useTaskVirtualization.ts:66/161 isTaskExpanded -> splitTaskIds's regular/summary/expanded bucketing, which drives TaskLayer.tsx:235 (<For expandedIds>) and both pooled lists. Result after migration: expanding or collapsing a task never re-renders the bars. Aggravating factor already present in 1.x — the call at line 161 is inside the untrack() opened at line 152, so splitTaskIds has no subscription to expansion either way and currently only refreshes incidentally.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: (1) Reassign instead of mutate: `setState(s => { const next = new Set(s.expandedTasks); next.has(id) ? next.delete(id) : next.add(id); s.expandedTasks = next; })` — replacing the property is what notifies for a non-proxied collection. (2) In useTaskVirtualization, hoist a real dependency out of the untrack: read `props.ganttConfig?.expandedTasks?.()` (or an expansion version accessor) next to `isSimpleMode()` at line 149 so splitTaskIds recomputes on expansion change; keep the per-id `checkExpanded` memoized map inside the untrack for cost.

syncHazards.description: `maxRegularCount` (line 206) and `maxSummaryCount` (line 227) are monotonic closure counters written from inside memo computes. rc.6 computes may run and have their result discarded (transition/optimistic re-runs, loading-boundary retries) — the discarded run still permanently raises the high-water mark, so the DOM pool grows on speculative work that was never committed. Also, since the counters live outside the reactive graph, any recompute ordering change between splitTaskIds and the pooled memos leaves pool size and content out of step for one flush (a stale pool slot renders a bar for a task that is no longer visible, since display:none is driven by the accessor value, not the pool length).
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Fold the high-water mark through the memo's own `prev` argument (rc.6 ComputeFunction receives prev): return `{ max, pool }` from a single createMemo and expose `() => memo().pool`. State then rolls back with the computation and the pool size is always derived from the same run that produced its contents.

syncHazards.description: pooledRegularTasks snapshots store proxies untracked (`untrack(() => ids.map(id => tasksObj[id]))`). taskStore.updateBarPosition replaces `state[id]` with a brand-new object, so the captured proxy can point at a detached raw object; this memo only re-runs when pooledRegularIds changes (i.e. on scroll/visibility), never on a position write. Under rc.6 the staleness window widens because writes land at flush rather than synchronously. Currently masked by Bar.tsx:113-117, which deliberately re-looks-up `props.taskStore.tasks[v.id]` instead of trusting the passed accessor.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Keep Bar's re-lookup (add a comment tying it to this memo so it is not 'simplified' during migration), or stop passing objects entirely and pass ids like pooledSummaryIds does, letting Bar own the single tracked store read.

syncHazards.description: handleTaskClickWithSelection writes the selection (sel.add / sel.toggle / sel.replace, lines 136-140) and then synchronously invokes props.onTaskClick (line 143) -> Gantt.tsx:482 handleTaskClick -> modals.showModal(taskId) and the host app's onTaskClick. Any consumer that reads selectionStore.selectedIds()/selectionCount() from that callback observes the PRE-click selection in rc.6. Note the setters themselves are safe: createSelectionStore uses functional updaters and rc.6 folds updaters against the staged value (dist/dev.js:4944).
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Pass the intended selection to the callback (`onTaskClick(taskId, event, nextIds)`) or have consumers read selection reactively rather than imperatively at callback time. If a synchronous read is unavoidable, wrap lines 136-143 in `flush(() => { ... })`.

syncHazards.description: handleCollectDependents reads `sel.isSelected(taskId)`, `sel.selectionCount()` and `sel.selectedIds()` (lines 110-114) from useBarDrag's onDragStart (useBarDrag.ts:84). Accessor reads return committed values under deferred writes. Safe today only because selection is written on click (mouseup, useBarDrag/Bar.tsx:248-251) and drag start is mousedown — i.e. a different tick. Any future 'select on mousedown' change turns this into a silently wrong batch-drag set.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: No change needed now; add a regression test that mousedown-select + drag in one gesture still batches the full selection, and prefer passing the selection snapshot into the drag-start payload rather than reading it inside the handler.

structuralConcerns: Pooling contract: both <Index> sites feed <For keyed={false}> SPARSE arrays (`new Array(poolSize)` at useTaskVirtualization.ts:208/229, and Array.prototype.map preserving holes at line 218). Before shipping, prove rc.6's non-keyed For (a) reads holes as undefined rather than skipping/truncating rows, and (b) reuses the row at index i in place — Index-equivalent pooling is load-bearing here: a remount tears down Bar's document-level mousemove/mouseup listeners mid-drag, which is exactly what the ID-based design at useTaskVirtualization.ts:99-100 exists to prevent.

The two closure caches (useTaskVirtualization.ts:70-96 and the copy in TaskLayerMinimal.tsx:45-73) and the two pool counters (lines 201-232) are hidden mutable state inside memo computes. rc.6 treats computes as pure and re-runnable, so this needs a redesign — derive from `prev` (pool counters) and from tracked Object.keys or a store revision signal (grouping cache) — not a local patch. This is the largest non-mechanical item in the batch.

Cross-batch dependency: ganttConfigStore's `expandedTasks` Set inside a createStore (mutated in place via produce) is unproxied in rc.6, and taskStore's produce/path setters (taskStore.ts:100 setTasks(id, obj), :110 produce, :129/:139 reconcile, :134 setTasks(id, undefined) as delete) must all be rewritten to the single draft form. useTaskVirtualization/TaskLayer are pure consumers of those, so their correctness cannot be validated until the store batch lands — sequence stores first, then this batch.

TaskLayer's constraint pipeline (handleConstrainPosition / handleResizeEnd / handleClampBatchDelta -> taskLayerConstraints.ts -> constraintEngine) is built on 1.x's synchronous read-your-own-write. Getting it right under deferred writes is an API change, not a rewrite of individual lines: geometry must flow forward as explicit arguments, and the read+cascade-write pair belongs inside one store draft. Decide this shape once, in the constraints batch, and have TaskLayer adopt it.

audits.summary: 4 files, 870 lines, 28 sites. Mechanical core is small and matches the advisory report: 3 <Index> -> <For keyed={false}> (TaskLayer.tsx:217,249; TaskLayerMinimal.tsx:130, callback shape identical so bodies are untouched), 2 import lines dropping the removed `Index` and moving `JSX` to @solidjs/web (TaskLayer.tsx:1, TaskLayerMinimal.tsx:1), and 4 createMemo(fn, initialValue, {equals}) -> createMemo(fn, {equals}) in createVirtualViewport.ts (50,69,107,124) which are provably behavior-preserving because no compute reads prev and rangeEquals is undefined-tolerant. useTaskVirtualization.ts needs no import changes at all. Beyond the report: 2 component-body STRICT_READ reads (TaskLayer.tsx:197-198, props resolved eagerly into useBoxSelect), a disputed advisory finding (useBoxSelect.ts:189 onCleanup is at hook top level under the component owner — no change needed), and three confirmations recorded to prevent over-migration (line 235's default <For>, the variable ref at 204, and user-level untrack over store proxies which does NOT emit STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED — that diagnostic requires an internal strictReadLabel). The real risk is not syntactic: 9 sync hazards, 3 high. (1) Both grouping caches invalidate on task-key COUNT (useTaskVirtualization.ts:78, TaskLayerMinimal.tsx:53) — 1.x flushed between unbatched writes so the memo saw intermediate counts; rc.6 coalesces a tick into one flush, so a same-tick add+remove leaves the cache permanently stale. (2) Bar.tsx writes updateBarPosition then calls onResizeEnd in the same handler, and TaskLayer.tsx:98 -> taskLayerConstraints.ts:87 re-reads getBarPosition for that bar, cascading successors from pre-write geometry. (3) ganttConfigStore mutates an `expandedTasks` Set in place inside a store; rc.6 does not proxy Sets, so expansion changes stop notifying splitTaskIds entirely. Plus the pool high-water counters (lines 206/227) are unrollbackable side effects in memo computes that should fold through `prev`. Sequence: stores batch first, then constraints API, then this batch.

syncHazards.description: Drop position is read from the store one tick stale. useDrag.handleMouseUp (useDrag.ts:160-163) runs the final onDragMove — which WRITES via taskStore.updateBarPosition (useBarDrag.ts:164/196-199/208) or batchMovePositions (line 149) — and then, still in the same synchronous stack, calls onDragEnd (useDrag.ts:177). onDragEnd's first act (useBarDrag.ts:271) is `deps.taskStore?.getBarPosition(t.id)`, which under deferred writes returns the PREVIOUSLY COMMITTED _bar. Both fallbacks are equally stale: `deps.x()` / `deps.width()` resolve to Bar.tsx:175/185, which read the same store proxy. The resulting {x, width} is handed to onDateChange -> Gantt.handleDateChange (Gantt.tsx:468-477) -> dateStore.xToDate, so the host application is told the task landed at the position it occupied one drag frame earlier. On a fast flick-and-release the error is the full final snap step (one columnWidth); with batchMovePositions every dependent task is reported wrong too. The inline comment on line 270 ('Read directly from store to avoid reactive timing issues') is precisely the assumption 2.0 invalidates.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Preferred: make onDragMove record what it wrote. Add `let lastGeom: { x: number; width: number } | null = null;` in useBarDrag, set it in each write branch (e.g. `lastGeom = { x: newX, width: originalWidth }` for dragging_bar, `{ x: newX, width: newWidth }` for dragging_left, `{ x: data.originalX as number, width: newWidth }` for dragging_right), reset it to null in onDragStart, and in onDragEnd use `const pos = lastGeom ?? deps.taskStore?.getBarPosition(t.id)`. Minimal alternative: `import { flush } from 'solid-js'` and call `flush()` in useDrag.ts immediately after the pendingMove block at line 163, which fixes this and the SummaryBar/onProgressChange hazards at once.

syncHazards.description: Progress drag reports the pre-drag percentage. In the same mouseup stack, the final onDragMove executes the dragging_progress branch and stages `updateTask(t.id, {...currentTask, progress: newProgress})` (line 252). onDragEnd then reads `t.progress` where `t = deps.taskInfo()` (line 261) — that accessor is Bar.tsx:207, `() => ({ id: t().id, progress: t().progress })`, which reads the `t` createMemo (Bar.tsx:134) which reads `taskStore.tasks[id].progress`. Deferred writes mean the memo still holds the committed value, so `onProgressChange(id, oldProgress)` fires. In 1.x the store write propagated synchronously and the memo recomputed on read, so this worked. Every progress drag now persists the wrong value to the host app.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Hoist the computed progress out of the dragging_progress branch: store it (`data['finalProgress'] = newProgress` at line 254, or a hook-local `lastProgress`) and report `deps.handlers.onProgressChange?.(t.id, (data['finalProgress'] as number) ?? t.progress)` at line 281. Do NOT rely on flush() alone here if you also adopt the draft-setter fix for updateTask, since either way passing the value explicitly is strictly more correct.

syncHazards.description: Keyboard resize computes its constraint cascade from the pre-resize width. Line 300 stages `updateBarPosition(taskId, { width: newWidth })`; line 302 then calls `onResizeEnd?.(taskId)` in the same synchronous handler. That resolves to TaskLayer.handleResizeEnd (TaskLayer.tsx:98-102) -> resolveResizeConstraints (utils/taskLayerConstraints.ts:83-105), whose first statement is `ctx.taskStore.getBarPosition?.(taskId)` and which then feeds `taskBar.x, taskBar.width` into resolveConstraints to compute and WRITE cascadeUpdates for every successor. Under deferred writes taskBar.width is the OLD width, so successors are pushed by the wrong amount — the bar grows but its dependents do not move, leaving a visibly violated finish-to-start link until some later unrelated write re-runs the cascade.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Either (a) `import { flush } from 'solid-js'` and call `flush()` between line 300 and line 302, or (b) better, change resolveResizeConstraints to take the new geometry explicitly — `resolveResizeConstraints(taskId, ctx, { x: x(), width: newWidth })` — and drop its internal getBarPosition read. Option (b) also fixes the equivalent stale read on the mouse-driven resize path via useBarDrag.ts:277-278.

syncHazards.description: Summary-bar drop resolves constraints against pre-drag descendant positions. useDrag.handleMouseUp runs the final onDragMove, which calls `props.taskStore.batchMovePositions(batchOriginals, deltaX)` at line 142 (staging a new x for the summary task and every descendant), and then invokes onDragEnd at line 146-150 in the same stack, which calls `props.onDragEnd?.(taskId())` = TaskLayer.handleResizeEnd -> resolveResizeConstraints -> getBarPosition. Every position it reads is the committed, pre-move value, so cascade updates for tasks depending on the summary group are computed from stale geometry and then written on top of the staged move — the two staged writes land in the same flush and the cascade wins for any successor it touches.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Same options as the useBarDrag hazard: `flush()` in useDrag.handleMouseUp after the final onDragMove (one fix covers Bar, SummaryBar and progress), or widen the onDragEnd contract to carry the applied deltaX so the constraint resolver can add it to the originals it already has in `data['batchOriginals']`.

syncHazards.description: Read-modify-write over the whole task object clobbers concurrently-staged writes. `const currentTask = deps.taskStore.getTask(t.id)` returns the committed store proxy; the branch then writes `updateTask(t.id, { ...currentTask, progress: newProgress })`, replacing the entire task entry. Under deferred writes, any change staged earlier in the same tick — most plausibly a `_bar` update from constrainTaskPosition's cascade (taskLayerConstraints.ts:69) or a sibling bar's batchMovePositions — is not visible in `currentTask` and is silently overwritten by the stale spread when both writes flush. Secondarily, spreading a store proxy copies the nested `_bar` PROXY reference back into the store rather than a plain object.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Add a narrow store action and stop round-tripping the whole task: in taskStore, `const setTaskProgress = (id: string, p: number) => setTasks(draft => { const t = draft[id]; if (t) t.progress = p; });` and call `deps.taskStore.setTaskProgress(t.id, newProgress)` here. This also removes the removed-API `setTasks(id, taskData)` path setter at taskStore.ts:100.

syncHazards.description: `onDateChange?.(taskId, { x: x(), width: newWidth })` reads x() from the store proxy AFTER the write staged on line 300. Today the write only carries `width`, so the committed x happens to equal the intended x and the reported value is correct by accident. The hazard is latent rather than active: it is the canonical write-then-read-same-path shape, and it breaks the moment updateBarPosition on this path also carries x (e.g. if shift-resize is ever extended to resize from the left edge, mirroring useBarDrag's dragging_left).
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Hoist the read above the write: `const curX = x();` before line 300, then `onDateChange?.(taskId, { x: curX, width: newWidth })`. Same treatment for `width()` at line 312 (hoist `const curW = width();` above line 311), where the risk is slightly higher because props.onConstrainPosition at line 307 can itself write _bar for this task via its cascade.

syncHazards.description: `setDragState('idle')` and `setIsDragging(false)` are staged at lines 183-184, but five call sites read `dragState()` as a synchronous control-flow guard: startDrag's re-entrancy check (line 196), handleMouseMove (line 130), handleMouseUp (line 155) and rafLoop (lines 79, 84). Any of these that executes before the microtask flush sees the stale non-idle state. The practical exposure is small — mousedown/mousemove/mouseup and rAF are all separate macrotasks with a flush in between — but a synthetic or programmatically-dispatched mousedown in the same task as a mouseup (Playwright force-click, dispatchEvent loops in tests) will be silently swallowed by line 196.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Keep the signals for rendering, but add a plain `let activeState: DragState = 'idle';` updated alongside every setDragState call, and use it for all five control-flow guards. This is more robust than flush() because it removes the timing dependency entirely from the state machine.

syncHazards.description: `deps.taskStore?.setDraggingTaskId?.(t.id)` stages the 'defer expensive recalculations' gate, then lines 96-101 immediately loop `deps.taskStore?.getBarPosition(id)` to snapshot originals, and line 263 stages `setDraggingTaskId(null)` before line 271 reads getBarPosition. Nothing downstream in either stack observes the new gate value. Currently benign (the gate only affects memos that recompute on later frames, and the originals snapshot genuinely wants the pre-drag positions), but it means the gate is not actually armed for anything that runs during the mousedown handler, and on drag end the gate re-opens one flush before the final geometry read.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: No code change strictly required; document the deferred semantics at both sites. If any consumer of draggingTaskId is later added to the same synchronous path, arm the gate with a plain module-level flag in taskStore in addition to the signal.

structuralConcerns: The entire drag pipeline is built on the assumption that store writes propagate synchronously, and it is stated as an explicit design intent in a comment (useBarDrag.ts:270 'Read directly from store to avoid reactive timing issues'). useDrag.handleMouseUp (useDrag.ts:160-177) deliberately runs the last onDragMove and then onDragEnd in one call stack so the end handler can observe the move's effect. In 2.0 that ordering is exactly wrong. This needs a contract change, not a local rewrite: onDragEnd must receive the geometry that onDragMove applied, rather than re-deriving it from the store. Recommendation: extend UseDragOptions so onDragMove can return/record an applied-state object that useDrag threads into onDragEnd, then delete every store read from useBarDrag.onDragEnd and SummaryBar.onDragEnd. A single flush() at useDrag.ts:163 is the cheap stopgap and fixes four of the eight hazards, but it papers over the inverted dependency.

Bar.tsx:108 + contexts/GanttEvents.tsx:23 is a hard blocker, not a warning. createContext<GanttEventHandlers>() with no default makes useContext throw ContextNotFoundError in 2.0 (verified in rc.6 client/core.d.ts:31 and :89-102), and useGanttEvents' `if (!context)` no-op fallback becomes unreachable dead code. Gantt.tsx never mounts GanttEventsProvider — only the three demo shells do — and BarDemo.tsx / ShowcaseDemo.tsx render <Bar> bare. So under rc.6 the library's primary render path throws during Bar setup. Fix is one line (createContext<GanttEventHandlers | null>(null)) but it must be scheduled first or nothing in this batch can be tested.

Bar.tsx's getTask() re-lookup (lines 110-118) exists solely to defeat <Index> snapshot pooling — the comment names <Index> explicitly. TaskLayer.tsx:217/249 is where those <Index> sites live (SMA-flagged) and they become <For keyed={false}>, whose callback still yields an item ACCESSOR, so the dual value-or-accessor handling in getTask() and in the taskPosition accessor at Bar.tsx:178-184 remains correct. Still, once TaskLayer migrates, re-validate whether the store re-lookup is still needed at all: if <For keyed={false}> hands down a live accessor over the store proxy, the re-lookup is now pure overhead on every x()/y()/width()/height() read (four store lookups per bar per frame).

SummaryBar.tsx:63 memoizes the raw _bar store proxy while Bar.tsx:171-174 documents deliberately NOT doing that. The two components disagree about the same problem. Today SummaryBar's memo happens to invalidate because taskStore replaces state[id] wholesale; the recommended 2.0 rewrite of updateBarPosition/batchMovePositions to draft mutations removes that whole-object churn and the memo stops invalidating. Rendering survives (proxy property reads still track in the consuming JSX effect) but the memo is then load-bearing-looking dead code and a trap for anyone who later adds snapshot()/deep()/an identity comparison to it. Align SummaryBar on Bar's pattern: read the fields directly, no memo over the proxy.

Eager memo creation is a per-bar cost multiplier. useBarConfig creates 7 memos per Bar (useBarConfig.ts:37-75) and Bar adds 4 more (lines 134, 335, 346, 370). In 1.x these were lazy; in 2.0 createMemo computes on creation, so a 1000-row chart performs ~11,000 eager computations at mount that previously happened on first read (and never at all for off-screen virtualized bars). Given this repo has an explicit perf posture (BarMinimal.tsx, GanttPerfIsolate.tsx, prof.start instrumentation), benchmark mount time after migration and apply { lazy: true } to the config memos if it regresses.

RowLayout.taskPositions is a Map (rowLayoutCalculator.ts:10) read through props in ExpandedTaskContainer.tsx:72, 84 and 121, and TaskLayer.tsx:39 holds a Map<string, RowLayout>. 2.0 does not proxy built-in collections. These are currently safe because they are memo outputs reassigned wholesale, but this is an invariant nobody has written down — add it as a comment or move to a plain object keyed by task id so the constraint is enforced by the type.
audits.summary:
Read all 5 batch files in full plus 5 followed helpers (useBarDrag.ts, useBarConfig.ts, useDrag.ts, contexts/GanttEvents.tsx, stores/taskStore.ts) and the consuming constraint utils. 40 sites, 8 sync hazards.

The purely mechanical surface is small: all five files need the same JSX-type import split (JSX is no longer exported from solid-js — confirmed against rc.6 types/index.d.ts; Show and For still are), and two tabIndex -> tabindex renames (rc.6 jsx.d.ts declares only lowercase tabindex, with no string index signature, so this is a build error). BarMinimal.tsx, SubtaskBar.tsx and ExpandedTaskContainer.tsx need NOTHING ELSE — their <Show> takes element children and their <For> is already the default keyed form whose callback shape is unchanged.

Two findings dominate. (1) A hard blocker the SMA missed entirely: Bar.tsx:108 calls useGanttEvents(), backed by a default-less createContext at GanttEvents.tsx:23. In 2.0 that throws ContextNotFoundError outside a provider, and Gantt.tsx never mounts GanttEventsProvider (only three demo shells do) while BarDemo/ShowcaseDemo render <Bar> bare — so every Bar in the primary render path throws on setup. One-line fix, must land first. (2) The drag pipeline is architecturally built on synchronous store propagation, with the assumption written down as a comment at useBarDrag.ts:270. useDrag.handleMouseUp deliberately runs the final onDragMove (which writes) and then onDragEnd (which re-reads the store) in one synchronous stack; under deferred writes the drop position (useBarDrag.ts:271), the drag-end progress (line 281), the keyboard-resize constraint cascade (Bar.tsx:302) and the summary-bar drop cascade (SummaryBar.tsx:148) are all one tick stale, silently persisting wrong dates and progress to the host app. A single flush() at useDrag.ts:163 fixes four of the eight hazards as a stopgap; the correct fix is to thread the applied geometry from onDragMove into onDragEnd and delete the store reads.

Also: useBarDrag.ts:250 does a whole-task read-modify-write that clobbers concurrently-staged writes; taskStore's updateBarPosition/batchMovePositions/updateTask/removeTask all use removed APIs (produce, path setters, undefined-as-delete), and the recommended draft-setter rewrite is what breaks SummaryBar.tsx:63's memo-over-a-store-proxy. topLevelReadCount is 8, all in one object literal at Bar.tsx:195-205, where they also genuinely freeze the handler set at setup.

SMA cross-check: sma-report.txt lists ZERO sites in the five batch files; its only entry touching anything I followed is useDrag.ts:250 (onCleanup), which I DISPUTE — onCleanup is still exported in rc.6 and valid at hook/component-owner scope. Everything else here is net-new.

syncHazards.description: positionMap's untrack(...) block suppresses every dependency on task data (verified: the store proxy's ownKeys trap DOES track — dev.js:9271 — so `for (const taskId in tasks)` would subscribe to the key set if it were not wrapped). The memo's only live dependencies are `props.taskStore` identity and `draggingTaskId()`. WRITE: any code path that stages tasks / _bar positions into the taskStore. READ: this memo, whose eager first run happens during ArrowLayer's component setup and reads the last COMMITTED store value. Under 1.x, a parent that wrote tasks synchronously before mounting ArrowLayer had those tasks visible on the memo's first run. Under 2.0 deferred writes, if the mount happens in the same synchronous run as the writes (createRoot body, an event handler, or a setup helper such as utils/ganttSetup), the first run sees the pre-flush state, `positions` is empty, `visibleDependencies` drops every dependency at line 139, and nothing ever re-triggers positionMap — the arrow layer stays permanently blank with no error and no warning.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Make the dependency real. Minimum: hoist the key-set read out of untrack — `const tasks = props.taskStore?.tasks; const ids = tasks ? Object.keys(tasks) : [];` (tracked via ownKeys) and iterate `ids` inside the untrack for the _bar reads. Better: delete the untrack entirely and let 2.0's flush coalesce the fine-grained _bar invalidations, which is what the untrack was hand-rolling in 1.x. If a manual trigger is preferred, adopt the ArrowLayerBatched positionVersion prop and read it as a used value, not `void`.

syncHazards.description: `void props.positionVersion;` is the sole tracked dependency that reflects bar movement, because both position reads (lines 139-140) are wrapped in untrack. WRITE: producers call taskStore.updateBarPosition / batchMovePositions and then separately bump the counter (GanttPerfIsolate.tsx:1529 `triggerArrowUpdate`, invoked at 1587 inside a `batch()` that must be deleted in 2.0). READ: this memo re-runs and calls getBarPosition. The 2.0 flush ordering is actually favourable — the counter write and the position writes land in the same flush, so the memo reads committed positions. The hazard is the two failure modes the protocol allows: (a) any producer that writes positions WITHOUT bumping the counter leaves the spatial index and arrowPathCache stale indefinitely, and (b) any caller that bumps the counter and then, in the same synchronous stack, reads arrow output (batchedPaths(), or measures the rendered <path> via getBoundingClientRect) gets pre-flush geometry, because the memo has not recomputed and the DOM has not been patched.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Delete the counter protocol: remove the untrack at lines 139-140 so getBarPosition subscribes normally, and drop line 123 plus the positionVersion prop (line 40). If the manual protocol must stay for perf, (1) change line 123 to a used read included in the memo's return value so it cannot be elided, (2) delete the now-removed `batch()` wrapper at the producer, and (3) require any synchronous read-back of arrow geometry to call `flush()` first.

syncHazards.description: Followed one level from both ArrowLayer and ArrowLayerBatched, which read positions through this store. `updateBarPosition` guards its write with a read of COMMITTED state: `if (!tasks[id]) return;` at line 108, before `setTasks(produce(...))` at line 110. Under 2.0 deferred writes, a setup or drag sequence that adds a task and sets its bar position in the same synchronous run has the task write still staged when the guard runs, so the guard sees undefined, returns early, and _bar is never written. getBarPosition then returns null (line 81), ArrowLayerBatched skips the relationship at line 141, and ArrowLayer's positionMap skips it at line 106 — arrows for freshly-created tasks silently never appear.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Move the existence check inside the draft, where staged state is visible: `setTasks(s => { const t = s[id]; if (!t?._bar) return; t._bar = { ...t._bar, ...position }; })`. This also removes the `produce` import (produce is deleted in 2.0 — its body IS the setter body now) and the path-setter forms at taskStore.ts:100/134.

syncHazards.description: While a drag is active ArrowLayer.tsx:158-159 passes positionMap={null}, so every Arrow falls back to this live per-endpoint `props.taskStore.getBarPosition(taskId)` read. WRITE: the pointermove handler stages _bar.x. READ: this call, and any constraint/snap/measurement code that runs later in the same handler. Under deferred writes both the read here and any getBoundingClientRect() on the arrow <path> in the same frame observe the pre-write geometry, because neither the store commit nor the DOM patch has happened yet. In 1.x the store commit was synchronous, so a drag handler could write and immediately re-read to derive a clamp or a cascade offset.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: In drag handlers, derive constraint/clamp math from the value about to be written rather than re-reading the store afterwards (pass the new x explicitly into resolveConstraints instead of calling getBarPosition again). Where a genuine post-write measurement is unavoidable, wrap it: `flush(); const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();`.

syncHazards.description: The spatialIndex memo invalidates module-level caches (arrowPathCache, lastVisibleSet, cachedResult) that a DIFFERENT memo, batchedPaths, both reads (lines 206-210, 229) and writes (lines 212, 232, 260). WRITE: spatialIndex clears the caches. READ: batchedPaths consults them. The ordering is correct today only because batchedPaths destructures spatialIndex() on its first line (169), forcing the clear to run first. In rc.6 memos are eager and scheduled at flush time; if anyone adds `{ lazy: true }`, reorders those reads, or reads batchedPaths() from a scope that has not pulled spatialIndex, batchedPaths serves paths generated from superseded positions. Independently, because the caches are module-scoped (lines 70-72), two mounted instances — or a Vite HMR reload, which preserves module state — cross-contaminate: instance B's mount clears instance A's cache and instance A's setsEqual short-circuit can return instance B's cachedResult.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Make the caches instance state and pass them through the dataflow rather than through module bindings: have spatialIndex return `{ index, positions, pathCache: new Map<number, ArrowPaths>() }` and let batchedPaths use `spatialIndex().pathCache` plus component-scoped `let lastVisibleSet / cachedResult` declared inside ArrowLayerBatched.

syncHazards.description: During a drag, positionMap returns the SAME Map reference it returned on the previous non-drag run (`cachedPositionsForFilter`, assigned at line 117). With the default memo comparator (isEqual / Object.is) an identical reference suppresses downstream notification, so visibleDependencies does not recompute. That is the intended freeze, and it un-freezes correctly when draggingTaskId flips back to null because the full branch then builds a fresh Map. The 2.0 change is only that the freeze and un-freeze edges now land at microtask flush boundaries rather than synchronously with the pointer event, so exactly one frame at each edge renders with the other side's position source.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Acceptable as-is if the one-frame edge is visually tolerable. If not, remove the dual-path sourcing (see structuralConcerns) so there is no source switch to be mistimed.

structuralConcerns: ArrowLayerBatched's module-level mutable caches (lines 70-72) are shared by every mounted instance and survive Vite HMR reloads, and they encode a cache-invalidation protocol split across two memos (spatialIndex clears at 125-128, batchedPaths reads/writes at 206-260). This needs to become instance state threaded through spatialIndex's return value, not a local rewrite. It is a pre-existing bug that 2.0's flush-time memo scheduling makes materially harder to reason about.

Both arrow layers replace real store tracking with hand-rolled dependency protocols: ArrowLayer wraps all task reads in untrack (line 103) and depends on nothing but draggingTaskId; ArrowLayerBatched wraps all position reads in untrack (139-140) and depends on a manually incremented positionVersion counter (123). These were 1.x workarounds for synchronous per-write propagation storms during scroll. Solid 2.0 already coalesces writes into a single microtask flush, which is the same optimization done correctly by the runtime. The migration should delete both untrack hacks and re-measure, rather than porting the workarounds; if a derived index is still wanted, `createStore(fn, seed, { key })` / createProjection is the 2.0-native shape for a reconciled spatial index.

ArrowLayer sources positions from two different reactive graphs depending on drag state (batched positionMap when idle, live per-Arrow getBarPosition when dragging — lines 157-160 feeding Arrow.tsx:181-187). In 2.0 the switch edge lands on a flush boundary, so the frames where draggingTaskId flips render with the outgoing source. Collapsing to one always-live derived source is now viable because the scheduler batches, and would remove the entire cachedPositionsForFilter mechanism.

Arrow.tsx's header comment (lines 1-2) records a deliberate decision to avoid createMemo because of 'reactive cascades that hurt scroll performance'. That cost model is 1.x-specific: rc.6 memos are eager/non-lazy by default with an explicit `{ lazy: true }` opt-in, and propagation is flush-scheduled. The decision's concrete cost is generatePath running three times per update (lines 244, 256, 258). Re-benchmark under rc.6 before carrying it forward.

None of the three files has any test coverage (tests/ contains no arrow tests; the only arrow-adjacent files are demos and examples/arrow.html). The two high-severity hazards here — untrack-hidden dependencies producing a silently blank arrow layer, and the stale existence guard in updateBarPosition — are exactly the failure class that produces no error and no warning at runtime. A regression test that mounts ArrowLayer against a taskStore populated in the same synchronous run, calls flush(), and asserts a non-empty positionMap should be written before the migration, not after.

The SMA report contains zero findings for any file in this batch (grep for 'components/Arrow' returns nothing; its only arrow-adjacent hits are src/demo/ArrowDemo.tsx:350 and src/entries/arrow.tsx:1, both outside this batch). Its rule set covers onMount, one-arg createEffect and createMemo initial values, none of which occur here — so it found nothing, and in particular missed all six JSX-namespace import sites, which are hard compile errors.
audits.summary: Three pure-render components with no effects, no onMount, no store writes, no context, no refs, no directives and no Index — so the mechanical surface is small and entirely import-shaped: six JSX-namespace sites (Arrow.tsx:4/178, ArrowLayer.tsx:1/59, ArrowLayerBatched.tsx:1/74) must move to `import type { JSX } from '@solidjs/web'`, plus tsconfig jsxImportSource and the vite-plugin-solid swap. For/createMemo/untrack all still ship from solid-js; the default keyed For overload, fragment children in For rows, SVG hyphenated attributes and undefined-removes-attribute all verified unchanged against rc.6 types, so every JSX element here is migration-inert. Zero top-level reactive reads in any component body. The real work is reactivity architecture, not syntax. Both layers deliberately hide their dependencies behind untrack — ArrowLayer.tsx:103 suppresses the store's ownKeys tracking (confirmed live in dev.js:9271) leaving positionMap dependent on nothing but draggingTaskId, and ArrowLayerBatched.tsx:139-140 suppresses every position read, leaving `void props.positionVersion` (123) as the sole live dependency. Combined with deferred writes this yields the batch's top hazard: ArrowLayer's eager first memo run reads pre-flush state and, having no task dependency, never recovers — the arrow layer renders permanently blank with no error, no warning and no test to catch it. A third high-severity hazard sits one level down in the helper both files read through: taskStore.updateBarPosition (108) guards a staged write with a committed-state read, so a task created and positioned in the same run never gets its _bar, and both layers then silently drop it (ArrowLayerBatched:141, ArrowLayer:106). Secondary: ArrowLayerBatched's module-level caches (70-72) are cross-instance and cross-HMR shared while two separate memos invalidate and consume them through those bindings. One notable free win — 2.0's write coalescing actually fixes a latent 1.x two-phase-load bug in taskCount(), so do not add a flush() between updateTasks and updateBarPosition.

structuralConcerns: ColumnPanel's cell-value model is the only real redesign in this batch. Row data is snapshotted once per row creation (line 202) and per cell (line 211) by reading a createStore proxy from inside a <For> callback body. Under rc.6 that scope carries strictRead='<For>', so every one of those store-proxy gets emits a STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED console.warn — O(visible rows x tasks) warnings per re-render, enough to make the dev console unusable on a large chart. Fixing it (row-level createMemo + inlining the cell expression into JSX) simultaneously repairs a pre-existing silent bug (panel cells never update when task data changes) but changes the ColumnDef.render contract: render(task, resourceId) becomes a function called inside a tracking scope on every dependency change, so it must be pure and must not create primitives. The two modal/popup pairs are the ones that meaningfully regress (they used to be gated behind <Show>) and are the right candidates for { lazy: true }.

Four of the five <For> lists in this batch (Grid 196, DateHeaders 212 and 229, ColumnPanel 200) iterate memos that allocate fresh objects on every recompute, so identity keying tears down and recreates every row owner on each viewport change.
