missed.description: No audit recorded the unproxied-Date invariant for the store that most directly holds Dates. `GanttConfigState` declares `ganttStart: Date` (line 35), `ganttEnd: Date` (36) and `ignoredDates: Date[]` (48), and all three are seeded into `createStore` here at 127-128 and 143. rc.6 does not proxy built-in collections, so in-place mutation notifies nothing. lib-stores-task raised exactly this as a `store-builtin-collection` site for taskStore's `_start`/`_end` (taskStore.ts:57) and lib-contexts-index raised it for types.ts:198, but lib-stores-config-date — which owns this file — flagged only `expandedTasks: Set<string>` (line 146) and left the Date fields unmentioned. It matters more here than in taskStore for two reasons. (1) `ganttStart`/`ganttEnd` are publicly settable through `GanttConfigStore.setGanttStart`/`setGanttEnd`, exported from index.ts:12. (2) lib-stores-config-date's own recommended makeSetter rewrite — `setState(s => { s[key] = typeof value === 'function' ? value(s[key]) : value; })` — hands `s.ganttStart`, a RAW unproxied Date, straight to a consumer-supplied updater function, which is precisely the shape that invites `d => { d.setHours(0); return d; }`. That would mutate in place, return a reference-equal Date, and notify nothing. Today all writes are whole-property reassignments (line 163, 217-220) so nothing is broken yet; the trap is created by the migration itself.
missed.rewrite: Record the invariant on GanttConfigState and enforce it in the makeSetter rewrite. Either normalise on write — `setState(s => { const next = typeof value === 'function' ? value(s[key]) : value; s[key] = next instanceof Date ? new Date(next.getTime()) : next; })` — or, cleaner, keep the two boundary Dates out of the store entirely and hold them as `createSignal<Date>` (the shape ganttDateStore.ts:69/72 already uses correctly), leaving the store for the scalar config only. Also document that `ignoredDates` (line 143) must be reassigned wholesale, never `push`ed, and that `getConfig()` returns its Date elements by reference.

missed.description: The public `onReady` contract silently narrows and no audit registered a fix. `onMount(() => props.onReady?.(api))` becomes `onSettled(...)`, and I verified in rc.6 that `onSettled` builds `createTrackedEffect(() => untrack(callback))` (signals dev.js:7217-7220) whose owner carries CONFIG_CHILDREN_FORBIDDEN — so the CONSUMER's `onReady` body may no longer create any reactive primitive (createSignal/createMemo/createEffect/createStore/createRoot) or call `onCleanup`; all of those throw. `onReady(api)` is the library's documented "here is your imperative handle, wire up your integration" hook (GanttProps.onReady), i.e. exactly the callback a consumer is most likely to use for setting up a derived signal or an effect over the returned api. lib-gantt mentioned the forbidden scope in passing inside a note whose primary prescription was an (incorrect — see disputed) untrack wrapper, and offered queueMicrotask only as an aside; it never made it the rewrite. Nothing else in the nine audits covers it.
missed.rewrite: onSettled(() => { const cb = props.onReady; if (cb) queueMicrotask(() => cb(api)); });  // no untrack needed — onSettled already runs its callback under untrack (dev.js:7220), so the props.onReady read creates no subscription and the effect has no deps, firing exactly once. The queueMicrotask defers the consumer callback out of the children-forbidden scope so onReady keeps its 1.x freedom to create primitives and register cleanup. Apply the same treatment to GanttContainer.tsx:187 (props.onContainerReady), whose current callee already creates six createEffects.

missed.description: Diagnostic leakage into consumer code, missed by every audit. When this effect is split as lib-gantt proposes, `props.onSelectionChange` moves into the apply half. I verified that rc.6's `runEffect` sets `prevStrictRead = setStrictRead("an effect callback")` immediately before invoking `node._effectFn` and only restores it in the `finally` (signals dev.js:6227-6256) — so strictRead is armed for the ENTIRE apply call stack, not just the library's own statements. The store proxy's get trap warns whenever `strictRead && !inDraft(target) && typeof key === 'string' && getObserver() === null` (dev.js:9147-9158). Consequence: any store-proxy read a CONSUMER performs inside `onSelectionChange` — e.g. `ids.forEach(id => taskStore.tasks[id]?.name)`, the obvious thing to write given `taskStore` is exported from index.ts:11 — emits `[STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED]` warnings that name the consumer's property, with no indication the library caused it. The same applies to any of `onDateChange`/`onProgressChange`/`onResizeEnd`/`onTaskClick` that end up invoked from an apply half. Several audits correctly note "reading a store proxy inside apply warns" for library code; none noticed the label propagates through the call stack into user callbacks.
missed.rewrite: Do not call consumer callbacks directly from apply. createEffect(() => ({ ids: selectionStore.selectedIds(), cb: props.onSelectionChange }), ({ ids, cb }) => { if (cb) queueMicrotask(() => cb(new Set(ids))); });  — the microtask hop clears both the strictRead label and the effect scope, so consumer code behaves exactly as it did in 1.x. Adopt this as the house rule for every public callback the library invokes from an effect apply, and note it on the GanttProps callback docs.

disputed.reason: lib-gantt is WRONG on the mechanism and the prescribed rewrite. It states: "onSettled is a TRACKED effect: the bare `props.onReady` read subscribes to prop identity and would re-fire onReady whenever the parent passes a new function literal (very common). Must untrack the prop read to preserve 'fire once'", and rewrites to `onSettled(() => { untrack(() => props.onReady)?.(api); })`. I read the published implementation: `function onSettled(callback) { ... createTrackedEffect(() => untrack(callback), { name: "onSettled" }) ... }` (@solidjs/signals 2.0.0-rc.6 dist/dev.js:7217-7220). The callback is already wrapped in `untrack`, so the body registers no dependencies, the effect has no sources, and it cannot re-fire on prop identity change. The untrack wrapper is dead code and the stated failure mode does not exist. This also contradicts lib-scroll-container, which states the opposite (correctly) for the same API at GanttContainer.tsx:170: "Reads inside the body are untracked (dev.js:7220 wraps the callback in untrack), so props.onContainerReady/props reads here do not create subscriptions." Two audits cite the same dev.js line and reach opposite conclusions; lib-scroll-container is right. The real defect at this line is the children-forbidden scope now imposed on the consumer's callback (filed under missed).

lib-gantt prescribes a `flush()` that is a documented no-op, so the bug it is meant to fix survives the migration. Its rewrite for this effect is `createEffect(() => ({...}), ({viewMode, tasks}, prev) => { ... dateStore.changeViewMode(viewMode); flush(); if (tasks?.length) runSetup(tasks); }, { defer: true })`, and its syncHazard for line 321 says "insert an explicit flush() between dateStore.changeViewMode(viewMode) and runSetup(tasks) so the reinit reads the committed new unit/step/columnWidth. flush() is legal here — apply runs from the scheduler with no owner." Verified against rc.6: `runEffect` calls `setEffectCallback(true)` before invoking the apply function (dist/dev.js:6229-6230), and `flush()` early-returns whenever `globalQueue._running`, emitting `[FLUSH_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK] flush() called from inside an effect callback is a no-op: the flush that runs effects is already in progress` (dist/dev.js:2279-2298). So the apply half gets a console warning and NO drain; `runSetup` still reads the stale, viewMode-derived `step()`/`unit()`/`columnWidth()` memos, which is exactly the Day→Month-renders-at-day-granularity bug the fix targets. lib-stores-config-date reached the correct conclusion on the same code path ("Do NOT reach for flush() here — changeViewMode is called from an effect at Gantt.tsx:321"), as did lib-stores-resource-selection ("flush() inside an effect callback is a no-op (FLUSH_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK)"). The correct fix is theirs: parse the incoming mode locally and thread step/unit into generateDates as explicit parameters. The `runtime` hint is also relevant: `flush(fn)` with a callback argument is likewise useless here, since its internal drain hits the same `_running` guard.

lib-scroll-container's fallback for syncHazard[0] is not a fallback — it throws. It writes: "or, as a last resort, call `flush()` between the write at 172 and the callback at 187." Both lines sit inside the `onMount` body at line 170, which the same audit migrates to `onSettled`. Verified: `onSettled` → `createTrackedEffect`, whose `run()` sets `setTrackedQueueCallback(true)` around `recompute(node)` (signals dev.js:6267-6275), and `flush()` throws unconditionally in that state: `if (inTrackedQueueCallback) { throw new Error("Cannot call flush() from inside onSettled or createTrackedEffect. flush() is not reentrant there. Writes made here are processed in the same flush's continuation; to force a drain afterwards, defer it: queueMicrotask(() => flush()).") }` (dist/dev.js:2279-2285). A reader who takes the stated last resort converts a silent zero-width viewport into a hard crash on first mount. The audit's two preferred options (derive viewportWidth from containerWidthSignal, or pass the measured numbers into the ContainerAPI object) are both correct and should be the only ones listed; the runtime itself supplies the third option in its error text — `queueMicrotask(() => flush())`.

lib-bars' #1-ranked finding rests on a false premise about this repo. It asserts "CRITICAL, definite runtime break … Gantt.tsx never mounts GanttEventsProvider (grep: only the three demo files do)" and, in its structuralConcerns, "under rc.6 every Bar in the main Gantt path throws on setup" and "must be scheduled first or nothing in this batch can be tested." That is wrong: Gantt.tsx:45 has `import { GanttEventsProvider } from '../contexts/GanttEvents';` and Gantt.tsx:540 renders `<GanttEventsProvider …>` as the component's JSX ROOT, closing at line 674 — it wraps `<GanttContainer>`, whose `barsLayer` prop carries `<TaskLayer>`, which renders `<Bar>` at TaskLayer.tsx:257. Because the `barsLayer` JSX is created where it is inserted (inside GanttContainer, itself a child of the provider), context resolution walks an owner chain that passes through the provider, so `useContext(GanttEventsContext)` returns the `handlers` object and `getContext`'s `isUndefined` throw (dev.js:5223-5225) never fires. The remaining exposure is real but much smaller and entirely outside this area: `src/demo/BarDemo.tsx:399` and `src/demo/ShowcaseDemo.tsx:1895/1924/1951/1978` render `<Bar>` with no provider, and external consumers could do the same. The `createContext<GanttEventHandlers | null>(null)` fix is still the right rc.6 shape and should be made — but it is not a blocker for the library render path and must not drive batch sequencing. By contrast the sibling claim for GanttStoresContext IS a genuine showstopper: Gantt.tsx:170 calls `useGanttStores()` unconditionally and Gantt mounts no GanttProvider around itself, so the bare `<Gantt tasks={…} />` form really does throw.

crossCutting: THE BRIEFED FACTS ARE WRONG ABOUT createRoot, AND ONLY TWO OF NINE AUDITS NOTICED. FACTS #2 lists "createRoot bodies" among the scopes where writes are allowed. I confirmed by reading the published runtime that this holds for STORE setters only: `devGuardStoreSetterWrite()` tests `if (context && !context._root && !(context._config & CONFIG_CHILDREN_FORBIDDEN))` with the comment "Roots are not owned computation scopes — setters inside createRoot bodies are legal" (@solidjs/signals 2.0.0-rc.6 dist/dev.js:4892-4909), whereas `setSignal`'s guard is `!(el._config & CONFIG_OWNED_WRITE) && !(context && context._config & CONFIG_CHILDREN_FORBIDDEN) && context && el._firewall !== context` — no `_root` branch at all (dev.js:4916-4930). A plain signal write inside a createRoot body therefore throws REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE. lib-stores-task and lib-stores-resource-selection each found this independently and flagged it as a deviation; the other seven inherited the FACTS wording. Consequence: the reflex "wrap the test in createRoot" is correct for taskStore's store writes and wrong for every signal-only store (selectionStore, resourceStore, ganttDateStore, useDrag, useBoxSelect, useGanttModals). Fix the FACTS document once, before any batch writes test code.

flush() LEGALITY IS SCOPE-DEPENDENT AND THE AUDITS GOT IT WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. There are three distinct behaviours in rc.6 and the nine audits collectively prescribe flush() in all three without distinguishing them: (a) LEGAL — event handlers, timers, promise continuations, plain test bodies (this covers lib-bars' useDrag.ts:163 fix, Bar.tsx:300→302, and every `flush()` in the three test files); (b) SILENT NO-OP + console warning — inside a createEffect/createRenderEffect apply callback, because `runEffect` sets `inEffectCallback = true` (dev.js:6229) and `flush()` returns early on `globalQueue._running` with `[FLUSH_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK]` (dev.js:2286-2298); (c) THROW — inside `onSettled` or `createTrackedEffect`, because `trackedEffect.run()` sets `inTrackedQueueCallback = true` (dev.js:6269) and `flush()` throws "not reentrant there" (dev.js:2280-2285). lib-gantt lands in (b), lib-scroll-container lands in (c), while lib-stores-config-date and lib-stores-resource-selection independently reached the right answer for the same code. Produce ONE table of the three cases in the migration guide and re-audit every "insert flush() here" recommendation against its caller's scope. The runtime supplies the escape hatch in its own error text for both (b) and (c): `queueMicrotask(() => flush())`.

onSettled HAS TWO SEPARATE CONSTRAINTS AND THE AUDITS EACH REMEMBERED ONLY ONE. The implementation is `createTrackedEffect(() => untrack(callback), { name: "onSettled" })` when an owner exists and is not children-forbidden, else a bare `globalQueue.enqueue` whose returned cleanup throws SETTLED_CLEANUP_UNOWNED (dev.js:7217-7239). So: (1) the BODY IS UNTRACKED — no prop read inside subscribes, and no defensive `untrack()` is needed (lib-scroll-container right, lib-gantt wrong); (2) the OWNER IS CHILDREN-FORBIDDEN — no primitive creation and no `onCleanup` anywhere in the body's call stack, return a cleanup instead. Both onSettled sites in this area hand control to a consumer callback (`props.onReady` at Gantt.tsx:234, `props.onContainerReady` at GanttContainer.tsx:187), so constraint (2) propagates into user code through public props. One shared rule covers all of it: never call a consumer callback synchronously from an onSettled body — defer with queueMicrotask, which restores the 1.x freedom for the consumer and costs nothing.

READ-YOUR-OWN-WRITE IS ONE ARCHITECTURE, NOT ~15 INDEPENDENT SITES, AND IT IS BEING FIXED INCONSISTENTLY. The same shape recurs across six batches: ganttDateStore.setupDates writes signals then ganttSetup.ts:69-84 reads them back; ganttSetup.ts:101 writes resources then reads the resourceIndexMap memo on 102; changeViewMode stages viewMode then generateDates reads the step()/unit() memos derived from it; useDrag runs the final onDragMove (which writes) then onDragEnd (which re-reads) in one stack; Bar.tsx:300 writes then :302 re-reads via resolveResizeConstraints; taskStore.updateBarPosition guards on a committed read before a staged write. Different audits proposed structurally different fixes for the same pattern — return-the-computed-value, thread-geometry-as-arguments, move-the-guard-into-the-draft, and flush() — and per the item above, two of the flush() variants do not work at all. Adopt ONE rule before touching any of them: producers return their computed values, consumers never read back state they just wrote, and store guards move inside the draft callback (the draft, unlike the outer proxy, does reflect staged state). Then the constraint/cascade layer (taskLayerConstraints, constraintEngine, useBarDrag, SummaryBar) can be migrated as a unit instead of site-by-site.

{ lazy: true } IS RECOMMENDED BY FOUR AUDITS BUT ONLY ONE STATES ITS SECOND EFFECT. MemoOptions.lazy exists in rc.6 (signals.d.ts:189) — that much is right — but its docstring reads: "When true, defers the initial computation until the value is first read, AND opts the memo into autodisposal — once it has no remaining subscribers it is torn down and recomputed from scratch on the next read. Non-lazy owned memos live for their owner's lifetime and never autodispose." lib-hooks flags the tradeoff; lib-chrome, lib-stores-config-date and lib-virtualization recommend it without it. That matters most exactly where it is being recommended: useBarConfig creates 7 memos per Bar and useTaskVirtualization/useGanttModals sit behind virtualized rows, so `lazy` trades a one-time mount cost for teardown-and-recompute churn every time a row scrolls out and back. Make this one measured decision across the ~25 affected memos rather than 25 local guesses; apply it unconditionally only to the genuinely rarely-read ones (showExpectedProgress, ignoredPositions, the modal/popup formatters behind <Show>).

BUILT-IN COLLECTIONS IN STORES IS THE REPO'S MOST-REPEATED TRAP AND THE CODEBASE ALREADY CONTAINS BOTH THE BUG AND THE FIX. Four audits describe it independently. The broken instance is ganttConfigStore's `expandedTasks: Set<string>` inside createStore, mutated in place through produce (lines 175-201) — unproxied, so expand/collapse notifies nothing and Gantt.tsx:371 plus useTaskVirtualization.ts:161 go dead. The correct pattern is already present three times: taskStore.collapsedTasks, resourceStore.collapsedGroups and selectionStore.selectedIds are all Sets held in signals and replaced immutably. Add to that the Date fields nobody flagged in ganttConfigStore (see missed). Write ONE invariant — built-ins inside a store are replace-only; prefer a signal holding an immutable collection, or Record<string, true> when per-key tracking is wanted — and encode it in types.ts alongside `expandedTasks?: Set<string>` (line 352) and the ProcessedTask Date fields (198, 216), which is where the public option shapes are declared.

<For> INSTALLS A STRICT-READ SCOPE THAT <Index> DID NOT, SO THE Index→For MIGRATION IMPORTS A NEW DIAGNOSTIC. I verified that solid-js dev.js:1174 sets `options.name = "<For>"` and mapArray then wraps the map callback in `setStrictRead(options.name)` / `setStrictRead(false)` (signals dev.js:11994-12005), so a store-proxy read taken directly in a For callback BODY (as opposed to inside JSX or a memo) hits the store get trap's `if (strictRead && !inDraft(target) && typeof key === 'string' && getObserver() === null)` and warns STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED (dev.js:9147-9158). lib-chrome found this and built its central ColumnPanel.tsx:202/211 finding on it; lib-virtualization, which owns the three <Index>→<For keyed={false}> conversions (TaskLayer.tsx:217/249, TaskLayerMinimal.tsx:130), describes the callback shape as "byte-identical" and does not mention that the replacement carries a strict-read label the original lacked. I checked all three bodies plus the other nine <For> sites in scope and every one is an expression-bodied arrow returning JSX, so nothing warns today — but the rule needs writing down before someone adds a `const task = store.tasks[id]` statement to a pooled row callback, which is precisely the shape that broke ColumnPanel.
critic.summary:
I re-ran every FACTS pattern over all 38 in-scope files and compared hit-by-hit against the nine audits. On raw site coverage they are close to complete: every removed/renamed symbol occurrence is claimed (20 JSX-namespace imports, 3 <Index>, 2 .Provider, 2 default-less createContext, 3 onMount, 3 onCleanup, 12 createEffect, 6 produce, 5 path setters, 2 reconcile, 1 batch, 1 createComputed, 4 three-arg createMemo, 5 refs), and all 37 SMA lines for in-scope files are covered. I found no unclaimed occurrence of any removed API. Two systematic sweeps confirmed the audits rather than extending them: a diff of the 1.x vs rc.6 jsx.d.ts attribute sets against every JSX attribute used in scope surfaces only `tabIndex` (3 sites, all already claimed — camelCase HTML aliases are gone, events keep camelCase), and an AST-ish scan for reactive mutators inside memo bodies found only plain local Set/Map writes already covered.

The value is therefore not in more sites but in four rewrites that contradict the runtime, which I verified by reading the published rc.6 dist rather than the FACTS. (1) lib-gantt's Gantt.tsx:234 claim that onSettled is tracked is false — `onSettled` is `createTrackedEffect(() => untrack(callback))` (dev.js:7220), so its prescribed untrack wrapper is dead code, and it directly contradicts lib-scroll-container's correct note on the same API. (2) lib-gantt prescribes `flush()` inside a createEffect apply callback at Gantt.tsx:316/321; `runEffect` sets `inEffectCallback=true` (dev.js:6229) and `flush()` returns early with a FLUSH_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK warning (dev.js:2286), so the stale-viewMode bug it targets survives the fix — while two sibling audits reached the right answer on the same code path. (3) lib-scroll-container's stated last resort of `flush()` between GanttContainer.tsx:172 and :187 sits inside onSettled, where flush THROWS (dev.js:2280); it converts a silent bug into a crash. (4) lib-bars' #1-ranked "showstopper" rests on "Gantt.tsx never mounts GanttEventsProvider" — it does, at Gantt.tsx:45/540, as the JSX root wrapping TaskLayer→Bar, so no Bar in the library path throws; the fix is still right but must not gate sequencing. The parallel GanttStores claim, by contrast, is a genuine showstopper.

Four genuine misses: the `useGanttEvents` public contract at index.ts:26 (the one index.ts export lib-contexts-index skipped while making exactly this decision for useGanttStores); unproxied `Date` fields inside ganttConfigStore's createStore, which the recommended makeSetter draft rewrite actively hands raw to consumer updaters; the children-forbidden scope that onSettled imposes on the public `onReady` callback; and strictRead propagating through a split effect's apply into consumer callbacks. Cross-cutting, the headline is that FACTS #2 is wrong — `setSignal` has no `_root` exemption where `devGuardStoreSetterWrite` does, so "wrap tests in createRoot" is right for stores and wrong for signals — a deviation only two audits caught and which should be corrected upstream before any batch writes test code.

If a write is ever added, it must live in an event handler/timer (component-body writes throw REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE) and the new value is only visible after the microtask flush.

structuralConcerns: No sync hazards exist in this batch: none of the four files performs a single signal or store write. syncHazards.description: onChange writes selectedScenario then, in the same synchronous handler, calls updateTasks() which reads allTasks() — a memo whose only dependency is selectedScenario() (line 628). Under deferred writes the signal write is staged, the memo has not recomputed, and allTasks() returns the PREVIOUS scenario's task list. taskStore.updateTasks then reconciles the store to the OLD tasks while <For each={allTasks()}> at line 900 (evaluated after the flush) renders the NEW tasks. Every new row's pos() lookup misses, so rect x/y/width are undefined and the newly selected scenario renders as invisible bars; the stale scenario's ids linger in the store. In 1.x the memo recomputed synchronously on read and this worked.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Delete the imperative pairing. Replace the onMount at 662 and the updateTasks helper at 667 with a split effect: createEffect(() => allTasks(), (tasks) => taskStore.updateTasks(tasks)) — compute reads the memo (tracked, write-free), apply does the store write (untracked, writes allowed). Then onChange becomes just setSelectedScenario(e.target.value), and the 'Reset Positions' button at 812 needs a separate explicit re-seed (e.g. taskStore.updateTasks(buildTasks(untrack(selectedScenario))) in the handler). If the imperative shape must be kept, insert flush() between the write and the read.

syncHazards.description: In the successor branch of resolveMovement, line 239 writes the predecessor's position via taskStore.updateBarPosition(otherTaskId, ...), and then line 251 (the maxDistance clamp) reads predTask._bar.x and predTask._bar.width off the same store proxy to compute newX. Under deferred writes that read returns the pre-write x, so the successor is clamped against where the predecessor USED to be. Line 248's guard also uses newDistance computed at line 220 from pre-write state. The same shape exists at 178 -> 190 (predecessor branch: push the successor, then read otherTask._bar.x for the maxDistance clamp) and at 203/264.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Make resolveMovement pure. Build a local Map<taskId, {x,y}> seeded lazily from taskStore.getBarPosition, have every read go through a getPos(id) helper that checks the map first, have every 'write' set the map entry, and return the accumulated updates. handleMouseMove then applies the whole plan in one taskStore.batchMovePositions / one setTasks(draft => ...) call. This is also strictly faster (one store notification per pointer move instead of N).

syncHazards.description: The `for (const rel of relationships)` loop at 143-272 re-reads each participant with taskStore.getTask(otherTaskId) (line 151) and then reads otherTask._bar / task._bar (159, 165, 171, 190, 215, 220, 226, 251, 257). A task written by an earlier iteration, or by a recursive resolveMovement frame at 169/194/230/255 (which itself writes at its own 178/203/239/264), is re-read at its stale committed value on the next iteration. Chains of three or more constrained tasks therefore converge one pointer-move behind instead of within a single move, and a task participating in two relationships can be positioned inconsistently.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Same fix as the previous hazard: a single working-copy map threaded through the recursion so reads see this move's accumulated decisions. Alternatively wrap the whole traversal in one setTasks(draft => { ... }) so every read goes through the draft, which DOES reflect staged state — but the traversal also reads via taskStore.getTask, so the map approach is cleaner and keeps the resolver testable without a store.

syncHazards.description: handleMouseMove calls resolveMovement (705) — which has already written successor/predecessor positions internally — and then writes the dragged task at 715 (single) or iterates result.updates at 720-722 (batch). result.x/result.y and every update in the batch were computed from reads taken before those internal writes. Ordering still resolves correctly (the outer write for taskId is staged last and wins), but the values themselves were derived from a pre-write snapshot, so a fixed-offset chain (scenario 6, chain-a/b/c) can drift by one frame during a fast drag.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Have resolveMovement return the complete update list and perform exactly one write here (taskStore.batchMovePositions or a single setTasks draft). No writes inside the resolver at all.

syncHazards.description: onConstrainPosition reads taskStore.getBarPosition(taskId) for the width, then resolveConstraints reads every neighbour position through context.getBarPosition/getTask (bound directly to the store), then lines 433 and 443 write the main task and each cascade successor. Within one invocation all reads precede all writes, so this is correct today. It becomes wrong the moment onConstrainPosition is invoked twice in one tick — which is exactly what a multi-select / batch drag would do, and what Bar.tsx:306 already does on the keyboard path if a caller ever stops returning null. The second call would resolve constraints against positions the first call staged but did not commit.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Pass the resolver an explicit position provider rather than binding it to the live store (context.getBarPosition = (id) => pendingPositions.get(id) ?? taskStore.getBarPosition(id)), and record every write into pendingPositions. Cheaper stopgap: assert/document that this callback is called at most once per tick, and add a flush() before re-entry if that assumption is ever violated.

syncHazards.description: toggleExpected reads showExpected() (line 193), then writes the local signal (194) and the config store (195) with the same explicitly-passed value. Correct as written because the read precedes both writes and the value is threaded by hand rather than re-read. Recorded because the shape is one edit away from breaking: any future `if (showExpected())` after line 194, or switching to setShowExpected(v => !v) followed by ganttConfig.setShowExpectedProgress(showExpected()), would read the stale committed value. The mirrored state (a local signal plus ganttConfig.showExpectedProgress) is what invites that edit.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Drop the local showExpected signal and read/write ganttConfig.showExpectedProgress() as the single source of truth: checked={ganttConfig.showExpectedProgress()} and onChange={(e) => ganttConfig.setShowExpectedProgress(e.target.checked)}. That removes both the duplicate write and the re-read temptation.

syncHazards.description: Twelve handlers use setConfig({ ...config(), key: value }) — read the whole config object, spread it, write it back (lines 481, 514, 530, 577, 604, 645, 680, 702, 720, 765, 797, 817). Each read precedes its own write and each handler is a separate macrotask, so no field is lost in normal interactive use. Under deferred writes, two of these firing before a flush (a test that dispatches two input events, or any programmatic 'apply preset' path) makes the second spread read the pre-first-write object and silently discard the first field.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: setConfig(prev => ({ ...prev, key: value })). Functional setters compose across staged writes in rc.6, so N updates in one tick all land.

syncHazards.description: updateBarPosition's early-return guard `if (!tasks[id]) return;` reads COMMITTED store state before entering the setter. Reached from ArrowDemo:392, BarDemo:433/443 and ConstraintDemo:178/203/239/264/715/721. If a seeding write (updateTasks/reconcile) and a position write ever land in the same tick — e.g. ConstraintDemo's onChange re-seeds and a queued pointer-move fires before the flush — the guard sees the pre-reconcile map, the id looks absent, and the position update is dropped with no error.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Move the existence check inside the draft callback, where staged state is visible: setTasks(state => { const task = state[id]; if (!task?._bar) return; Object.assign(task._bar, position); }).

structuralConcerns: ConstraintDemo's resolveMovement (lines 90-275) is the one function in this batch that genuinely needs a redesign rather than a local rewrite. It is a recursive constraint solver that interleaves taskStore reads and taskStore.updateBarPosition writes across loop iterations and recursion depths, and its correctness depends entirely on 1.x's synchronous write propagation. Rewrite it as a pure planner over a local Map<taskId,{x,y}> working copy (reads fall through to taskStore.getBarPosition on first touch, writes only touch the map) that returns the full update set; handleMouseMove then applies it in one write. This also removes N store notifications per pointer move.

ConstraintDemo maintains store state through two disconnected imperative paths — an onMount seed (662) and a manually-called updateTasks() (667, invoked from onChange at 779 and onClick at 812) — while allTasks() is already a memo of selectedScenario. The whole arrangement should collapse into one split createEffect(() => allTasks(), taskStore.updateTasks). That single change deletes the highest-severity hazard in the batch instead of patching it with flush().

All three demos are blocked on the taskStore.ts migration: createStore's setter is used exclusively through removed APIs (produce at 110 and 161, path setters at 100, setTasks(id, undefined) at 134, reconcile at 129/139). No demo file can be migrated independently — taskStore must land first, and its updateBarPosition guard (line 108, committed-state read outside the draft) has to move inside the draft as part of that work.

ganttConfigStore.makeSetter (151-166) is a Setter<T> emulation over a store path that both computes `prev` from committed state and returns committed state after the write. Under deferred writes both halves are wrong. BarDemo only rides one of its twenty products (setShowExpectedProgress) with a plain value, so this batch survives a naive port — but the shim's public type (Setter<GanttConfigState[K]>) is a lie in 2.0 and should be narrowed to (v: T | ((prev: T) => T)) => void so no caller can depend on the return value.

The Index -> For keyed={false} swap at BarDemo:397 is mechanical at the call site, but the comment on line 395 ('use Index instead of For to prevent component recreation on position updates') encodes a real pooling assumption: Bar instances must survive position writes. keyed={false} preserves exactly that model, but it is worth a runtime check that Bar's internal memos and useBarDrag state are not torn down when allTasks() returns a fresh array after a reconcile.

BarDemo's debug overlay (460-529) reads the store non-reactively inside a For child body. 2.0 emits no warning (mapArray untracks without a strict-read label) so this will not surface during migration testing — it just quietly renders stale or empty coordinates. Worth fixing to thunks while the file is open, matching ConstraintDemo:902 and ArrowDemo:1034.

All three files carry `// @ts-nocheck` on line 1. TypeScript will not flag the removed Index/onMount imports, the new For keyed overloads, or the StoreSetter signature change in this batch, so a green tsc proves nothing here. Remove the directive during the migration and fix the fallout, or these files will be the last place the 2.0 breakages surface.

The demos import '../stores/taskStore.js' and '../stores/ganttConfigStore.js' while the files on disk are .ts. That resolution is provided by Vite today; confirm @solidjs/vite-plugin@3.0.0-next.35 (native compiler by default) preserves the .js -> .ts extension rewrite before assuming these files even load.
audits.summary:
Read all three files in full (1347 + 663 + 1186 lines) plus, one level down, taskStore.ts, ganttConfigStore.ts (makeSetter) and constraintEngine.ts (pure, no Solid imports). 32 sites, 8 sync hazards, 8 structural concerns.

MECHANICAL CORE (small): 3 import lines (each imports removed symbols from 'solid-js'; the package itself does not move — there is no solid-js/web or solid-js/store import and no JSX type import in any of the three, since all carry // @ts-nocheck), 3 onMount -> onSettled, 1 Index -> For keyed={false}. All four SMA findings for this batch (ArrowDemo:350, BarDemo:173, BarDemo:397, ConstraintDemo:662) are confirmed; I dispute none. Two dead imports the SMA missed: createMemo in ArrowDemo:2 and onCleanup in ConstraintDemo:2. All three onMount bodies are clean for onSettled's children-forbidden scope — no onCleanup, no primitives created directly or through taskStore.updateTasks, no async work — and since onSettled wraps its callback in an unlabeled untrack (signals dev.js:7220) it runs once and emits no STRICT_READ, so onMount -> onSettled is a true rename here.

WHAT THE SMA MISSED, AND WHY THIS BATCH IS M NOT S: every store write in all three demos routes through taskStore.ts, which uses produce (110, 161), path setters (100), setTasks(id, undefined) (134) and reconcile (129, 139) — none of which survive rc.6. No demo can be migrated before that store lands. And ConstraintDemo:777-779 is a hard break, not a warning: setSelectedScenario(v) followed synchronously by updateTasks(), which reads allTasks() — a memo of selectedScenario. Under deferred writes the memo has not recomputed, so the store is seeded with the OLD scenario while <For each={allTasks()}> renders the NEW one; every new row's pos() misses and the scenario renders as invisible bars. ConstraintDemo's resolveMovement (90-275) is the structural one: a recursive solver that interleaves store reads with four updateBarPosition writes (178, 203, 239, 264) across loop iterations and recursion depths — line 239 writes a predecessor and line 251 reads that same predecessor's _bar back to clamp newX. It needs a pure-planner rewrite over a local working copy, not a local patch.

Everything else is quieter. ArrowDemo is nearly clean: one onMount, twelve setConfig({...config(), k}) read-modify-writes that are safe per-event but should become functional setters, no read-after-write in either drag handler. BarDemo's onConstrainPosition creates no primitives and is called from unowned event scopes, so it is safe today — but it resolves constraints against the live store, which breaks the moment it is called twice in a tick. taskStore's `if (!tasks[id]) return` guard (line 108) reads committed state outside the draft and will silently drop position writes that share a tick with a reconcile.

No classList, use:, on:/oncapture:, attr:/bool:, /*@once*/, ref callbacks, Context.Provider, createResource, batch, on(), createComputed, mergeProps/splitProps, unwrap, Dynamic, render, @solid-primitives usage or tests anywhere in this batch. Two createMemo calls, both 1-arg, so the (fn, initialValue, options) reshape does not bite. topLevelReadCount is 2 (BarDemo:462 and :478) and both are inside a For child body, not a component body — the actual component bodies of all three files contain zero top-level reactive reads, and ConstraintDemo:902 / ArrowDemo:1034 already use the correct thunk pattern.

syncHazards.description: HAZARD #1 (name): `setTaskConfig('name', e.target.value)` at 1084 is immediately followed by `updateTaskA()` at 1085, and updateTaskA (665-678) reads `taskConfig.name` at line 670 to build the object it writes into taskStore. Under deferred writes the store read at 670 still returns the PREVIOUS committed name, so every keystroke writes the stale name into taskStore and <Bar task={{name: taskConfig.name}}> (1898) and the task store permanently disagree by one edit; on the first keystroke the bar keeps the old name forever until another keystroke arrives.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Stop round-tripping through the store: give updateTaskA a patch parameter - `const updateTaskA = (patch = {}) => { const prev = snapshot(taskStore.getTask('task-a')); taskStore.updateTask('task-a', { ...prev, name: taskConfig.name, ..., ...patch }); }` and call `updateTaskA({ name: e.target.value })`. Cleanest: delete updateTaskA entirely and replace it with a split createEffect - compute reads taskConfig.name/progress/color/colorProgress/locked/invalid into a plain object, apply writes taskStore.updateTask (apply may write and is untracked). A one-line stopgap is `flush()` between the setter and updateTaskA(), which is legal inside an event handler.

syncHazards.description: HAZARD #2 (color): `setTaskConfig('color', ...)` at 1097 then `updateTaskA()` at 1098, which reads `taskConfig.color` at 672. Stale by one edit - the color swatch (JSX, reactive) updates but the stored task keeps the previous color.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Same as hazard #1: pass the new value explicitly (`updateTaskA({ color: e.target.value })`) or derive taskStore's task-a from taskConfig with a split createEffect.

syncHazards.description: HAZARD #3 (colorProgress): `setTaskConfig('colorProgress', ...)` at 1115-1118 then `updateTaskA()` at 1119, which reads `taskConfig.colorProgress` at 673. Stale by one edit.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Same as hazard #1: `updateTaskA({ colorProgress: e.target.value })`.

syncHazards.description: HAZARD #4 (progress): `setTaskConfig('progress', parseInt(...))` at 1138-1141 then `updateTaskA()` at 1142, which reads `taskConfig.progress` at 671. On a range input this fires continuously, so the stored progress trails the slider by exactly one input event - and when dragging stops, the last value is never committed to taskStore.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Same as hazard #1: `updateTaskA({ progress: parseInt(e.target.value) })`, or derive via split createEffect so the trailing value is always applied.

syncHazards.description: HAZARD #5 (locked): `setTaskConfig('locked', e.target.checked)` at 1188-1191 then `updateTaskA()` at 1192, which reads `taskConfig.locked` at 674 into `constraints: { locked }`. The checkbox flips but taskStore keeps the OPPOSITE lock state, so drag/constraint behaviour (resolveConstraints reads task.constraints.locked via context.getTask) is inverted relative to the UI until the next toggle.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Same as hazard #1: `updateTaskA({ constraints: { locked: e.target.checked } })`. This one is a behaviour inversion, not just a display lag - fix it before shipping.

syncHazards.description: HAZARD #6 (invalid): `setTaskConfig('invalid', e.target.checked)` at 1213-1216 then `updateTaskA()` at 1217, which reads `taskConfig.invalid` at 675. Stale by one toggle.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Same as hazard #1: `updateTaskA({ invalid: e.target.checked })`.

syncHazards.description: HAZARD #7 (Task B locked): `setTaskBConfig('locked', e.target.checked)` at 1775 then `updateTaskB()` at 1776, which reads `taskBConfig.locked` at 690. Same inverted-lock-state failure as hazard #5, for task-b.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Give updateTaskB a patch parameter and call `updateTaskB({ constraints: { locked: e.target.checked } })`, or derive task-b from taskBConfig with a split createEffect.

syncHazards.description: HAZARD #8 (applyPreset clobbers the preset positions): lines 807-826 call taskStore.updateBarPosition for task-a..task-d (each stages a draft write that rewrites state[id]._bar). Line 829 then reads `taskStore.getTask('task-a')`, which under deferred writes returns the task with the OLD _bar, and line 831 writes it back with `setTasks('task-a', {...taskA, ...})` - a whole-node replacement that overwrites the staged _bar. Result: clicking any preset button updates colors/names but the bars stay at their previous x positions, i.e. every preset that moves bars (constrained, fixedOffset, startToStart, finishToFinish) silently stops working.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Do the field update and the position update in ONE draft write, e.g. `setTasks(d => { const t = d['task-a']; Object.assign(t, {name: preset.taskConfig.name, progress: ..., color: ..., colorProgress: ..., invalid: ...}); t.constraints.locked = preset.taskConfig.locked; Object.assign(t._bar, {...positions['task-a'], y: 70, height: 30}); })` - add a taskStore method that takes (id, patch, barPatch). Failing that, reorder so all updateTask calls precede all updateBarPosition calls, or call flush() at line 828 (legal inside this click handler).

syncHazards.description: HAZARD #9 (same clobber for tasks B/C/D): `taskStore.getTask('task-b')` at 843 (and 'task-c' at 854, 'task-d' at 865) read committed state after the staged updateBarPosition writes at 812/817/822, then lines 845/856/867 write the stale `{...taskX}` back as a whole-node replacement, discarding the new _bar for all three tasks.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Same fix as hazard #8, applied to task-b/task-c/task-d: fold the position reset and the field reset into a single draft write per task (or one draft write for all four).

syncHazards.description: HAZARD #10 (resize-end constraint cascade): handleResizeEnd reads `taskStore.getBarPosition(taskId)` at 910 and feeds taskBar.x/taskBar.width into resolveConstraints at 919-924. Its caller Bar.tsx:300 writes the new width (`props.taskStore?.updateBarPosition(taskId, { width: newWidth })`) and then calls onResizeEnd on line 302 in the SAME synchronous handler (keyboard shift+Arrow resize). Under deferred writes handleResizeEnd sees the pre-resize width, so the cascade positions the successors for the OLD duration and the chain visibly lags one keystroke behind.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Change the onResizeEnd contract to pass the new geometry: `onResizeEnd(taskId, { x, width })` (Bar.tsx already has newWidth in scope) and have handleResizeEnd use the passed values instead of re-reading the store. If the contract must stay, call flush() at the top of handleResizeEnd - it runs from an event handler so flush() is legal there.

syncHazards.description: HAZARD #11 (constraint cascade reads committed positions): handleConstrainPosition reads `taskStore.getBarPosition(taskId)` at 880 and resolveConstraints re-reads every predecessor/successor position through `context.getBarPosition` (885) while the cascade loop at 899-902 stages writes for those same successors. Within one pointermove this is still correct (useBarDrag.ts:155-164 calls onConstrainPosition BEFORE its own updateBarPosition), but any caller that writes a position and then calls onConstrainPosition in the same tick - or two constrain calls in one tick, e.g. auto-repeat on Bar.tsx:307 - resolves against stale geometry and produces a cascade that undershoots by one step.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Pass the authoritative geometry into the callback instead of re-reading the store (onConstrainPosition(taskId, newX, newY, {width}) - Bar/useBarDrag already know the width), and build the constraint context from a snapshot() taken once per gesture rather than from live store getters. Do not add flush() inside the drag path; it would force a full settle per pointermove.

structuralConcerns: The core pattern of this demo - 'write config store, then synchronously read that same config store to mirror it into taskStore' (updateTaskA at 665-678 and updateTaskB at 681-693, invoked from 7 input handlers) - is exactly what deferred writes break, and it cannot be fixed by a local rename. Replace the two imperative mirrors with two split createEffects: compute reads taskConfig/taskBConfig fields and returns a PLAIN object (never the store proxy - reading a proxy in apply warns STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED), apply calls taskStore.updateTask. That also deletes 7 hazard sites at once and makes the mirror correct for preset changes too (applyPreset currently duplicates the same mirroring logic inline at 828-875 precisely because the effect-less design forces it).

taskStore.updateTask(id, taskData) (taskStore.ts:99-101 -> setTasks(id, taskData)) is a WHOLE-NODE REPLACEMENT API. Every one of this file's 6 call sites builds the replacement from `{...taskA}` - a shallow spread of the live store proxy. Under deferred writes any write to that task staged earlier in the same tick (a bar position, a drag delta) is silently discarded by the replacement. The API should become a patch-merge performed inside the draft (setTasks(d => { Object.assign(d[id], patch) })) before this file is migrated; otherwise hazards #8/#9 will keep reappearing in new call sites.

Seeding via lifecycle is avoidable. initializeTasks (613-658) exists only to fill the task store once; converting onMount -> onSettled preserves it but keeps a write-from-a-lifecycle-hook and a one-settle window where getBarPosition returns null (the arrow fallbacks at 960-987 paper over it with duplicated hardcoded coordinates). Prefer passing the initial task array to createTaskStore() so the store is born populated; then onSettled/onMount disappear, the duplicated fallback literals at 960-987 can go, and there is no lifecycle write at all. Note that calling initializeTasks() directly in the component body is NOT an option - a store write during component setup throws REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE in 2.0 dev.

The onConstrainPosition / onResizeEnd callback contract (Bar -> useBarDrag -> this file) assumes synchronous propagation: the callee re-reads the store to discover what the caller just wrote. Under deferred writes the contract must carry the geometry in its arguments. This is a cross-file API change (Bar.tsx:295-313, useBarDrag.ts:143-190/260-283, GanttEvents.tsx, TaskLayer.tsx, Gantt.tsx all implement the same signature), so it needs to be decided once for the whole repo rather than patched per demo.

createGanttConfigStore is instantiated at line 546 and never used. It should be deleted here, but note that keeping it anywhere in the repo requires migrating two 2.0-breaking constructs inside ganttConfigStore.ts: the makeSetter shim (returns Setter<T>, computes prev from committed state and returns state[key] after the write - both semantics are unrepresentable under deferred writes) and setState('expandedTasks', produce(set => ...)) (produce is removed, and Set is not proxied in 2.0 so in-place mutation notifies nothing; the property must be reassigned to a new Set).

Passing accessors (popupVisible, popupPosition, hoveredTask, modalTask, relationships) as props to TaskDataPopup/TaskDataModal still works, but hoveredTask/modalTask (595-606) return the live store PROXY from taskStore.getTask. If those children read the proxy inside a createEffect apply callback they will emit STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED in 2.0 dev; the memos should return snapshot(task) (or the children must do their reads in compute).
audits.summary: Read all 2030 lines plus the delegated helpers (taskStore.ts createTaskStore: getTask/getBarPosition/updateTask/updateBarPosition/updateTasks; ganttConfigStore.ts createGanttConfigStore; constraintEngine.ts resolveConstraints - pure) and the call sites in Bar.tsx / useBarDrag.ts that invoke this file's callbacks. 55 sites: 5 import-level changes (onMount, onCleanup, batch specifiers, solid-js/store -> solid-js, and the @ts-nocheck that will hide all of it), 7 createStore declarations whose setters change shape, 1 onMount -> onSettled, 1 batch removal, 31 path setters setX('key', v) and 7 object-merge setters setX(obj) that must all become draft callbacks, 1 store-proxy spread (6 lines), and 1 dead createGanttConfigStore call. No Index/Show-callback/Context.Provider/classList/ref/use:/Dynamic/render/createEffect/createComputed/on()/produce/unwrap/mergeProps/splitProps/createResource in this file, and zero top-level reactive reads (all reads are inside memos, JSX or event handlers). syncHazards.description: handleConstrainResize writes the dragged task at L1645 (updateBarPosition -> setTasks draft, setting startHours AND durationHours) and then, in the same synchronous call, reads the store back through calculateCascadeUpdates(taskId, finalX, context) at L1648. That helper (src/utils/constraintEngine.ts:554) calls context.getBarPosition = mockTaskStore.getBarPosition (L1537), which reads tasks[id].startHours/durationHours. In 1.x the store write was already applied, so predecessor bars carried the NEW width; in rc.6 the write is staged until the microtask flush, so the read returns the previous width. The helper seeds updates.set(taskId,{x:newX}) so the x is fine, but FS/SF successor minima are computed as predBar.x + predBar.width (getMinSuccessorX), so every cascaded successor is placed with the stale width. Because useDrag drives this once per animation frame, the error from the FINAL frame is never corrected and persists after mouseup.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Move the cascade computation above the write and feed the new geometry explicitly: const cascadeCtx = { ...context, getBarPosition: (id) => id === taskId ? { ...mockTaskStore.getBarPosition(id), x: finalX, width: finalWidth } : mockTaskStore.getBarPosition(id) }; const cascadeUpdates = calculateCascadeUpdates(taskId, finalX, cascadeCtx); then updateBarPosition(taskId, { x: finalX, width: finalWidth }); then the cascade loop; then triggerArrowUpdate(). Do NOT reach for flush() here — it would force a full settle inside a 60fps rAF loop.

syncHazards.description: startDrag's re-entrancy guard reads dragState() at L196 and the same function stages the write at L218-219 (setDragState/setIsDragging); handleMouseUp mirrors this with the guard at L155 and the writes at L183-184. Under deferred writes, a second startDrag dispatched inside the SAME synchronous event still observes 'idle', so it passes the guard, overwrites dragData and installs a second pair of document mousemove/mouseup listeners. Every bar variant in this batch routes mousedown through startDrag (L382, L403, L417, L448, L524, L545, L559, L617, L641, L655, L716-720, L1231-1235, L1389-1393); today only e.stopPropagation() in the child handles prevents a double dispatch, so the guard is load-bearing and now unreliable.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Back the guard with a plain closure boolean that flips synchronously (let active = false; if (active) return; active = true; ... set active = false in handleMouseUp) and keep dragState/isDragging purely for rendering; alternatively call flush() immediately after setDragState in startDrag. Cross-file: fix must land with the useDrag batch, but this demo is one of its main consumers.

syncHazards.description: The onMount body calls updateSize() at L1767, which writes viewportWidth/viewportHeight/positionVersion, and then starts the autoTest rAF loop whose tick() reads totalWidth() and viewportWidth() (L1779-1780) — values derived from those very writes. It is safe only because rAF runs in a later task, after the microtask flush; the moment anyone converts the first tick to a synchronous call, or reads viewportWidth()/totalWidth() directly in the onSettled body, they will get the 1200/800 defaults instead of the measured container size and the auto-scroll bounds will be wrong.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Capture the measured size into locals inside updateSize and pass them to tick(), or keep the rAF indirection and add a comment that the read must not be hoisted into the onSettled body.

syncHazards.description: handleConstrainPosition is correct as written (all store reads — mockTaskStore.getBarPosition at L1557 and every read inside resolveConstraints at L1574 — happen strictly before the writes at L1581/L1585), but it is one edit away from the L1648 bug: the constraint context it builds at L1564-1571 hands the engine a LIVE store reader, so any future statement placed after a write in this function silently reads pre-write positions. The same applies if a multi-select drag ever calls handleConstrainPosition twice within one frame: the second call would read the first call's uncommitted positions and the two would fight.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Keep the reads-before-writes ordering and document it; if batch/multi-task drags are added, thread a per-tick override map (the pattern calculateCascadeUpdates already uses with its `updates` map) into getBarPosition instead of re-reading the store.

structuralConcerns: Context redesign, not a local rewrite: 8 useGanttEvents() call sites (L434, 500, 576, 672, 754, 836, 918, 1282) rely on useContext returning undefined outside a provider, and 6 of them are NOT covered by the auto-wrap rule at L1468-1470 (experiments/nochildren/contained/willchange/combined/dragconst). In rc.6 useContext throws ContextNotFoundError (verified in solid-js 2.0.0-rc.6 dist/dev.js: useContext -> getContext -> throw when the resolved value is undefined). Fixing it properly means changing createContext<GanttEventHandlers>() to a null default in src/contexts/GanttEvents.tsx, which touches every other consumer of that context; the cheap demo-local alternative is to always render <GanttEventsProvider> at L2086.

useDrag coupling: 12 of the 17 bar variants instantiate useDrag in their component bodies. Its top-level onCleanup (src/hooks/useDrag.ts:250) stays legal (component-owned scope), but its state machine assumes synchronous signal propagation for its re-entrancy guards (see syncHazards). This demo cannot be migrated or perf-tested independently of the useDrag migration.

Eager memos invalidate the harness's purpose: this file exists to isolate per-primitive rendering cost, and in 2.0 memos are non-lazy by default. The 10 never-read dummy memos (L1714-1753) plus every per-bar `t` memo now compute at creation and live for the owner's lifetime, so all recorded 1.x baselines (?bar=, ?memos=, ?virt=) must be re-measured rather than compared. Adding { lazy: true } restores 1.x shape but not 1.x scheduling.

Dead/broken variants should be deleted or normalized before migrating: BarMinimal, BarWithText, BarWithHandles, BarReactive, BarWithDrag, BarWithEvents and BarFull treat props.task as a plain object, but the <For> at L2038 passes an accessor (`task={() => tasks[task.id]}`). They are already broken in 1.x (`task._bar` is undefined) and in 2.0 they additionally emit STRICT_READ warnings. V8-V17 use the `typeof props.task === 'function' ? props.task() : props.task` shape; converging on that (or on a plain store row) removes all 6 top-level reads at once.

Tooling/verification gap: the file is `// @ts-nocheck` (L1), so none of the type-level breakage (JSX namespace move, StoreSetter signature, removed exports) will surface at build time — this batch must be validated by actually loading the page for each ?bar= variant. Also needs the repo-level moves: vite-plugin-solid -> @solidjs/vite-plugin 3.0.0-next.35 and tsconfig jsxImportSource -> '@solidjs/web'. Note that under @solidjs/vite-plugin's vitest posture, test.environment 'node' resolves the SERVER build (no subscription graph), so any smoke test of this component must stay on jsdom.

Drag pipeline timing: all position writes now land on the microtask flush rather than inside the rAF callback. Functionally this is an improvement (one flush per frame instead of per-setter work), but it means the DOM transform for a dragged bar is applied after the rAF callback returns rather than during it; if the perf traces in this repo assert on within-frame ordering (rAF -> style write), they will need re-baselining.
audits.summary: GanttPerfIsolate.tsx (2093 lines, 17 bar variants + one 640-line main component) needs 4 import fixes (onMount, Index, batch removed from the 'solid-js' block at L2-11; 'solid-js/store' -> 'solid-js' with produce dropped at L12), one produce->draft-setter rewrite (L1516, the file's only store write path), two batch removals (L1580, L1644), and one onMount->onSettled conversion (L1758) whose body must return a merged cleanup for both the resize listener (L1769) and the currently-uncancelled rAF loop (L1806). All five SMA findings for this file are confirmed; I add ~25 sites it missed. The two highest-value findings are not import-level: (1) a deferred-write break at L1645->L1648, where handleConstrainResize writes the dragged bar and then calls calculateCascadeUpdates, which reads the bar's width back through the live store reader mockTaskStore.getBarPosition — every cascaded successor gets positioned with the previous frame's width and the last frame's error persists after mouseup; (2) createContext<GanttEventHandlers>() with no default (src/contexts/GanttEvents.tsx:23) makes useGanttEvents() throw ContextNotFoundError for the 6 bar variants that are not auto-wrapped by the L1468-1470 gate — including ?bar=dragconst, the variant this file's own header text advertises. The batch note's hover-zone suspicion is cleared: setHoverZone (L1220-1222 / L1367-1369) is write-only in the mousemove handler and is only read from JSX via getCursor(), so there is no same-stack read-after-write there. Writes are otherwise all owner-free (DOM handlers / rAF) or inside onSettled, so no REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE throws; no createEffect, no on(), no createComputed, no Index/Suspense/classList/use:/attr: usage; all 20 createMemo calls are single-argument. Six STRICT_READ top-level prop/store reads sit in three already-broken legacy variants.

syncHazards.description: runStressTest uses the reactive signal `running()` as its own start/stop latch: it reads running() at L898 and writes setRunning(true) at L905 / setRunning(false) at L901 and L929. Under deferred writes running() returns the last committed value, so a second entry before the microtask flush (the autoTest timer at L982 racing a user click on V-Scroll/H-Scroll/Both at L1089/1102/1115, a double click, or the Stop button at L1070 followed immediately by a start) still sees the pre-write value: two RAF tick loops can be started against a single `stressAbort` controller (L893/L907-908), and the first loop then becomes unstoppable because stressAbort only points at the second controller.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Make the latch non-reactive: `let isRunning = false;` (or test `stressAbort !== null`) for the guard at L898 and for the early-return, and keep setRunning()/setTestMode() purely as UI mirrors. Alternatively call flush() immediately after setRunning(true) — but a plain flag is cheaper and removes the race entirely.

syncHazards.description: Followed one level from GanttExperiments.tsx:254/344/444. startDrag writes setDragState(state) (L218) and setIsDragging(true) (L219) and then, still in the same synchronous mousedown stack, calls onDragStart?.(dragData, state) at L221. Any consumer callback that reads dragState() or isDragging() to learn the new state gets the stale 'idle'/false under deferred writes. The demo's callbacks are no-ops (L255-257 etc.) so this batch is unaffected, but the same hook backs the real bar drag code.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Consumers must use the `state` argument that is already passed to onDragStart rather than reading the hook's signals; if a consumer genuinely needs the committed value, call flush() before invoking onDragStart, or mirror the state into a plain `let currentState` that the hook reads internally.

syncHazards.description: Re-entrancy guard `if (dragState() !== 'idle') return;` (L196) reads a value that the same function writes at L218. Two startDrag calls in one tick both observe 'idle' and both install document mousemove/mouseup listeners (L224-225) while overwriting dragData (L209). In this batch the nested resize-handle handlers call e.stopPropagation() first (L289, L303, L377, L391, L481, L495), so only one fires per event — the hazard is latent, not live.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Track drag activity in a plain closure variable (dragData !== null already serves) and keep dragState()/isDragging() as render-only mirrors.

syncHazards.description: Measurement-model shift rather than a correctness bug: the stress tick (L927-961) sets scrollArea.scrollTop/scrollLeft, the browser scroll event reaches GanttContainer.handleScroll (GanttContainer.tsx:152) which calls this onScroll, which writes setScrollX/setScrollY. In 1.x the dependent memos (visibleRowRange L573, visibleXRange L586, the nine mode memos) and the bar DOM writes ran synchronously inside that handler; in 2.0 they run at the microtask flush after it. Any profiling this harness exists to produce (per-frame cost attributed to the scroll handler) is measuring a different boundary after the port, and read-after-write patterns added later in this handler would silently see stale scroll values.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: If 1.x-comparable numbers are needed, import flush from 'solid-js' and call flush() at the end of the tick (L959) or of the onScroll callback so the recompute lands inside the measured frame; otherwise re-baseline all recorded timings and note the flush boundary in the harness docs.

syncHazards.description: The Stop button sets the plain flag `stressAbort.abort = true` (immediate) and then setRunning(false)/setTestMode(null) (deferred). The RAF tick (L928-931) independently writes the same two signals when it observes the abort flag. The button/label swap driven by `running() ?` at L1068 therefore happens one microtask after the click, and two writers race for the same tick. Idempotent here (both write false/null), so it is a timing artefact only.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: No change required; if the one-frame UI lag matters, derive the button label from the same plain flag used for the L898 guard, or flush() after the write in the click handler.

structuralConcerns: Memo eagerness invalidates this harness's premise. rc.6 memos are non-lazy by default (MemoOptions.lazy, signals.d.ts:180-189, is opt-in), so all nine mode-guarded memos (L598, 621, 635, 659, 706, 722, 745, 752, 776, 797, 824, 852) now compute at component setup instead of only when the selected mode reads them. Each early-returns after reading virtMode(), so the standing subscription set stays small, but every virtMode change re-runs all of them and the 1.x 'unselected memos never execute' assumption that this file was written to exploit is gone. Adding { lazy: true } restores 1.x laziness but also opts each memo into autodisposal — which is incompatible with the cached-closure variants below.

The smartCache (L652-698) and cachedVisibleTasks (L596-599) experiments store incremental state in closure variables mutated from inside memo computes. That was already against the rules in 1.x and is explicitly contrary to the 2.0 compute contract; it does not throw (the writes are plain JS, not reactive), but it cannot be combined with { lazy: true } autodisposal and its correctness now depends on undocumented recompute ordering. These two variants need to be redesigned as a two-stage derived chain (which is what the xySplit variant at L621/L635 already is) or moved into a split createEffect apply before the numbers they produce mean anything.

The 'splitEquals' experiment (L702-749) never actually had custom equality under solid-js 1.9 — the 2-arg createMemo passed { equals: idsEqual } as the initial value. The port turns that argument into real options, so this variant changes behavior with a zero-line diff. Every recorded comparison between 'splitEquals' and the other modes must be re-measured after migration, and the team should decide whether the intended experiment was 'custom equality' or 'ID-array staging without equality' (the latter now needs the option removed).

Deferred writes move the entire scroll -> signal -> memo -> DOM pipeline out of the scroll/RAF callback and into the microtask flush. For a file whose only purpose is DevTools frame profiling, this is a harness-design change, not a code change: either insert flush() at the end of the RAF tick to keep work inside the measured frame, or restructure the harness to measure to the flush boundary and re-baseline every stored result.

Index pooling assumption in DateHeadersOptimized: <For keyed={false}> preserves Index's slot pooling exactly, but only the lower header (numeric slots, L26-34) benefits. upperSlots (L38-95) allocates fresh objects per recompute, so every pooled upper slot's accessor changes identity on every scroll tick and re-runs its bindings — the component's documented 'zero DOM churn' guarantee is half true today and stays half true after the port. Consider memoising the slot objects by (startIndex,text) or expressing the pool with the new <Repeat count>.

Optional-provider context pattern: useGanttEvents (GanttEvents.tsx:53-66) returns no-op handlers when the context is missing. createContext<T>() with no default throws in 2.0, so that whole fallback is unreachable and the three bar variants here (L225/321/409) become provider-mandatory. Give the context the no-op handler object as its real default before migrating any consumer.

Out-of-batch blockers for actually running this demo: src/entries/experiments.tsx:1 imports render from 'solid-js/web' (must become '@solidjs/web'); package.json:85 still pins vite-plugin-solid ^2.11.12 and :101 solid-js ^1.9.12; tsconfig.json:8 sets jsxImportSource 'solid-js' and must become '@solidjs/web'. Until those move, nothing in this batch can be validated at runtime.

Both files are // @ts-nocheck, so the type-level half of this migration (JSX namespace relocation, For keyed overloads, DynamicProps, StoreReturn) produces zero diagnostics. Recommend removing @ts-nocheck for the duration of the port and re-adding it only if the pre-existing untyped props are not worth fixing.
audits.summary: Read both files in full (1217 + 240 lines) plus the two helpers they delegate to (hooks/useDrag.ts, contexts/GanttEvents.tsx). 36 sites. Mechanical core: 4 import changes (Dynamic -> @solidjs/web, createStore -> solid-js, onMount -> onSettled, Index -> For), 3 <Index> -> <For keyed={false}> conversions whose callback shapes are already correct, and one onMount/onCleanup pair -> onSettled with a returned cleanup (the body creates no Solid primitives directly or through callees, and both of its writers - a setTimeout and a ResizeObserver callback - are unowned, so it is a legal onSettled body; the two timers should also be cleared in the cleanup). Highest-value finding, which the advisory report mis-classified: the two 'createMemo initial value' hits at L706 and L722 are not initial values at all - they are already options-shaped, which means under solid-js 1.9 the { equals: idsEqual } object was silently swallowed as `prev` and the splitEquals experiment ran with NO custom equality; porting to rc.6 activates that equality with a zero-line diff and changes what the harness measures. The demo never writes its store (createStore setter is discarded), so there are no store-path/produce/reconcile/unwrap sites and no store-side deferred-write exposure; the sync hazards are all signal-latch shaped - runStressTest using running() as its own start/stop guard (medium) and useDrag calling onDragStart after writing dragState/isDragging (medium, latent here because the demo passes no-op callbacks). Structurally, the real cost is not the rewrite but the harness: rc.6 memos are eager by default, two experiment variants keep incremental caches inside memo computes, and every timing this file records moves from inline-in-the-scroll-handler to the microtask flush.

syncHazards.description: startFpsCounter() is @solid-primitives/raf's start(), whose body is `if (running()) return; setRunning(true); requestAnimationFrame(loop)`. It is invoked from inside onMount -> onSettled, which in rc.6 is a TRACKED effect. Two failures compound: (1) the running() read subscribes the onSettled bundle to createRAF's internal signal and the setRunning(true) in the same body dirties it, so after the microtask flush the whole onSettled body re-runs and loadTasks() executes a second time (setTasks re-applied, renderTime and domStats measured twice, benchmark numbers polluted); (2) the read-then-write guard itself is evaluated against COMMITTED state, so if start() is ever reached twice before a flush it starts two RAF loops.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: onSettled(() => { untrack(() => { loadTasks(); startFpsCounter(); }); }); - untrack removes the subscription while writes stay legal in an onSettled body. Belt and braces: guard with a plain `let fpsStarted = false` closure latch so re-entry does not depend on committed signal state.

syncHazards.description: startDrag guards re-entry with `if (dragState() !== 'idle') return;` (196) and only then writes setDragState(state) (218) / setIsDragging(true) (219). Under deferred writes the setter stages the value, so a second startDrag reached in the SAME synchronous dispatch still reads the committed 'idle', passes the guard, overwrites dragData (209-216) and registers a second pair of document mousemove/mouseup listeners. GanttMinimalTest reaches exactly this shape: TestBar's resize handles (206-213) and the bar's own onMouseDown (203) both call startDrag from one delegated mousedown dispatch, relying on e.stopPropagation() plus this guard.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Back the guard with non-reactive state: `let active = false; if (active) return; active = true; ...`, clear it in handleMouseUp alongside setDragState('idle'), and keep dragState()/isDragging() purely for rendering. Same treatment for the `dragState() !== 'idle'` checks at 130 and 155.

syncHazards.description: loadTasks() takes a timestamp, calls setTasks(calendarData.tasks), then measures the resulting render by reading the DOM (document.querySelectorAll('.bar-wrapper') at 325 and '.arrow-layer > g' at 326). In 1.x the write rendered synchronously; in rc.6 it is staged and rendered on the microtask flush, so the measured value changes meaning (it now includes scheduler latency) even though the double requestAnimationFrame + setTimeout(0) still guarantees the reads land after the flush.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Either keep the double-RAF (correct, just re-baseline the numbers) or make the boundary explicit: `setTasks(...); await flush(); requestAnimationFrame(() => ...)` so the report separates flush time from paint time.

syncHazards.description: startProfile sets setRecording(true) (83) and immediately schedules countFrames (92), whose first statement reads recording() (87); runScrollTest (118-161) additionally calls startProfile() and then runs scroll() synchronously. The read happens in a RAF callback, which runs after the microtask flush, so the committed value is already true - correct today, but the pattern is one refactor away from breaking (e.g. if countFrames were ever invoked synchronously instead of scheduled).
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Pass the intent explicitly instead of round-tripping through the signal: give countFrames a plain `let isRecording = true` closure flag cleared in stopProfile next to setRecording(false), and keep the recording() signal for rendering only.

structuralConcerns: createMemo is EAGER (non-lazy) by default in rc.6. This batch exists to measure Solid's reactive cost, so the change invalidates its baselines: GanttMinimalTest creates one t() memo per visible bar (151) plus five window memos (277/280/292/299/306), and benchmarks/profiler/instrumentation/memoTracker.js is built around counting pull-driven memo invocations. Decide per memo whether to pass { lazy: true } for 1.x parity or to re-baseline; either way analyzeMemos' CHEAP/EXPENSIVE/CASCADE thresholds (memoTracker.js:218-221) and its per-frame cascade grouping (176-205) now describe a different scheduler.

Frame attribution changes across all three demos: signal writes made from RAF callbacks (GanttMinimalTest measureFrame 442-468, GanttPerfDemo createRAF callback 64-105, GanttProfiler countFrames 86-91) are staged, and the resulting DOM patches run on the microtask flush after the callback returns. Work that used to appear inside the RAF task in a trace now appears in a trailing microtask - the FPS / worst-frame / avg-frame figures these demos print, and the Chrome traces the bench scripts capture, must be re-baselined rather than compared to 1.x runs.

onMount -> onSettled is not a pure rename here: onSettled is a tracked, children-forbidden effect. Each of the four bodies in this batch (GanttMinimalTest:417, GanttPerfDemo:269 and :334, GanttProfiler:165) must be audited for (a) synchronous reactive reads, which now create subscriptions that re-run the whole body - GanttPerfDemo:334 already trips this through createRAF's start(); (b) onCleanup calls, which throw and must become a single returned disposer; (c) primitive creation, directly or through any helper/callback invoked from the body.

benchmarks/profiler/index.js mixes ESM exports with CommonJS require() in createBenchmarkRunner (71-82) and window.__ganttPerf (241). Those paths throw ReferenceError today in the browser and will keep throwing after the migration; anyone verifying the perf demos post-migration via window.__ganttPerf or createBenchmarkRunner will misread it as a Solid 2 regression. Fix it in the same pass using the static imports the module already has.

The three demos cannot boot until src/entries/minimal-test.tsx, src/entries/perf.tsx and src/entries/profiler.tsx switch `import { render } from 'solid-js/web'` to '@solidjs/web' (one line each), tsconfig sets jsxImportSource '@solidjs/web', and config/vite/{solid,demo}.js swaps vite-plugin-solid ^2.11.12 for @solidjs/vite-plugin 3.0.0-next.35 (babel-preset-solid ^1.9.12 can then be dropped from devDependencies). Those files are outside this batch but gate any runtime verification of it.

GanttProfiler's instrumentStore (41-73) monkey-patches window.__ganttTaskStore.getBarPosition/getTask/updateBarPosition. Under deferred store writes, updateBarPosition returns before the store commits, so the wall-clock the profiler attributes to that method no longer includes the propagation it triggers - that cost moves into the scheduler flush and is invisible to the callTree instrumentation. If the tool's purpose is finding hot reactive paths it needs an extra hook around the flush, or it will systematically under-report writes and over-report the first read after a flush.

GanttMinimalTest stores Date instances inside createStore (initialTasks spread at 121 from parsedTasks 94-98). rc.6 does not proxy Date/Map/Set, so any future in-place mutation of task._start/_end notifies nothing. Normalise to epoch numbers (or keep the dates outside the store) while the file is being touched.
audits.summary: 35 sites: 31 in the five listed files plus 4 in delegated helpers (3 in src/contexts/GanttEvents.tsx reached from GanttMinimalTest, 1 hazard in src/hooks/useDrag.ts). All 11 sma-report entries for this batch are reproduced and agreed with; the SMA missed the removed-symbol import lines (GanttMinimalTest:2 onMount+Index, GanttPerfDemo:2, GanttProfiler:2), the eager-memo behaviour change that invalidates this batch's entire purpose, the Date instances held in createStore, the top-level Object.keys(store) STRICT_READ, the dead ref on <Gantt>, the ESM/require defects in benchmarks/profiler/index.js, the createMemo prev-argument forwarding in memoTracker, the context provider/default sites the demos depend on, and - most importantly - that GanttPerfDemo:334's onSettled body reads a signal through @solid-primitives/raf's start(), which makes the body re-run and loadTasks() fire twice. Mechanical work is small: 5 import lines, 4 onMount -> onSettled with 4 onCleanup -> returned disposers, 1 Index -> For keyed={false}, 1 three-arg createMemo. The real cost is behavioural - deferred writes push RAF-driven DOM patches into a trailing microtask and eager memos change what the profiler measures, so every number these demos produce needs re-baselining - and @solid-primitives/raf must go to 4.0.0-next.2 or nothing in GanttPerfDemo resolves.
