syncHazards.description: onDateChange runs synchronously inside the mouseup call stack (useDrag.ts:159-177 drains the pending move, writing every dragged/batch-moved bar's _bar via taskStore.updateBarPosition/batchMovePositions, then calls onDragEnd -> useBarDrag.ts:263-275 -> Gantt.handleDateChange:467-476 -> this handler). It then READS taskStore.tasks[id]._bar.x/.width for every task to compute dxPx/dwPx against lastX/lastWidth. Under deferred writes the final drag frame's writes are still staged, so every bar reports its previous position: the PATCHed start/end silently omit the last frame of movement, and any dependent that only moved on that final frame fails the `Math.abs(dxPx) < 0.5` test at line 210 and gets no PATCH at all. If the user drags and releases within a single RAF frame the whole gesture can be discarded ('produced no PATCH (no Δ)').
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Call flush() (exported from solid-js) as the first statement of onDateChange — the handler is unowned, so flush is allowed — before the `for (const id of Object.keys(taskStore.tasks))` loop. Structurally better: change the Gantt/useBarDrag contract so onDragEnd captures the final {x, width} it just wrote and passes them down, instead of every consumer re-reading the store.

syncHazards.description: After `await Promise.all(patches.map(api.patchTask))` the microtask flush has run, so `taskStore.tasks[p.id]._bar` here returns the COMMITTED final position, while the delta that produced the persisted start/end was computed at lines 196-212 from the pre-flush (stale) position. lastX/lastWidth are therefore re-based to a pixel position that does not correspond to dbState's dates, so the next drag's delta is off by exactly the frame lost in the previous drag — the error compounds across drags.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Record the exact values used for the delta: push `{ id, start, end, x: bar.x, width: bar.width }` in the loop at line 219 and, after the PATCH, do `lastX.set(p.id, p.x); lastWidth.set(p.id, p.width);` instead of re-reading the store. (Combine with the flush() fix so both reads agree.)

syncHazards.description: refetch stages setBundle(data) at line 93 and then relies on `queueMicrotask(snapshotChartX)` to observe the re-processed bar positions. In 2.0 the bundle write commits in the scheduled flush, during which Gantt's createEffect (src/components/Gantt.tsx:288-303) calls runSetup -> initializeTasks -> taskStore writes that produce the new _bar values. A single queued microtask is no longer a guarantee that those effect-phase store writes have committed, so lastX/lastWidth can be snapshotted from the OLD layout; the first drag after a refetch then computes its delta against stale baselines and PATCHes wrong dates.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: queueMicrotask(() => { flush(); snapshotChartX(); }) — or move the snapshot behind a setTimeout(…, 0) like the onReady path, with flush() inside. Long term, have the Gantt expose a post-settle 'layout ready' callback carrying the positions instead of scraping window.__ganttTaskStore.

syncHazards.description: updateConstraint computes the next ConstraintRow from a committed read of constraints() and writes the whole object back. With staged writes, two calls in the same synchronous turn (a paste/auto-fill that sets several constraint fields, a future 'clear constraints' helper, or any programmatic multi-field patch) both read the same pre-flush value and the earlier write is silently lost.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: setConstraints((prev) => ({ ...prev, [key]: value })) — functional updaters compose against the staged value.

syncHazards.description: updateDep (and addDep at 257, removeDep at 263) rebuild the deps array from a committed deps() read. The rendered rows only reflect a staged write after the flush, so any second mutation issued in the same turn — e.g. a handler that changes maxMode and resets maxValue, or two onInput events dispatched in one task during tests — is computed against the pre-write array and clobbers the first.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: setDeps((prev) => prev.map((d, i) => (i === idx ? { ...d, ...patch } : d))); apply the same functional-updater form to addDep and removeDep.

syncHazards.description: setDragVersion bumps the invalidation counter that the selectedTask memo (line 117) depends on; the memo, the <Show when={selectedTask()}> subtree and TaskForm's reset effect now all run on the following flush rather than on the next lazy read. The edit panel therefore shows the pre-drag start/end for one microtask after a drag-PATCH, and if the user is mid-typing when a drag-PATCH lands the deferred reset overwrites the in-flight edits slightly later than it used to.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: No code change needed for correctness; if the panel must be consistent before the handler returns, add flush() after the setDragVersion/dbState updates. Consider guarding the reset effect so it does not clobber a dirty form.

syncHazards.description: handleSubmit sets setSubmitting(true) and immediately awaits props.onSubmit, reading id()/name()/start()/end()/progress()/resource()/color()/constraints()/deps() in the same turn. Those are different signals from the one written, so no value is stale today — but the `disabled={submitting()}` DOM update now lands on the flush rather than synchronously, so a synchronous double-submit (double Enter in the same task) is no longer blocked by the disabled attribute.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Guard re-entrancy with a plain boolean local (`let inFlight = false`) in addition to the submitting() signal, or flush() right after setSubmitting(true).

structuralConcerns: DbDemo's entire drag->PATCH strategy is built on synchronous store commits: it scrapes window.__ganttTaskStore.tasks[id]._bar (a live store proxy exposed at src/components/Gantt.tsx:238) at three different points in the drag/refetch lifecycle and diffs pixel positions across them. Under 2.0 every one of those reads sits on a different side of a flush boundary. Sprinkling flush() makes it work, but the durable fix is an API change in the Gantt: onDragEnd already holds the exact final {x, width} it wrote (useBarDrag.ts:270-273) and Gantt.handleDateChange already converts them (Gantt.tsx:467-476) — pass the positions (or precise dates) through onDateChange so the demo never has to re-read the store.

DbDemo's timing cannot be validated until the Gantt batch is fixed: Gantt.tsx runs runSetup (which performs taskStore/resourceStore/dateStore writes) inside onMount (line 287) and inside a single-argument createEffect body under untrack (lines 288-303, 305-329). Both throw REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE in 2.0 dev (untrack does not clear the owner), and the fix chosen there determines when _bar values commit relative to DbDemo's queueMicrotask/setTimeout snapshots.

taskStore itself (src/stores/taskStore.ts) uses the removed store APIs that DbDemo depends on for _bar semantics: produce (lines 111-120, 160-172), path setter setTasks(id, taskData) (line 101), setTasks(id, undefined) as a delete (line 135), reconcile at the root (lines 128, 139), plus a Set held in a signal for collapsedTasks. Those rewrites can change the granularity/ordering of _bar notifications that DbDemo's delta diffing observes.

TaskForm mirrors props.initial into ten local signals and re-syncs them from a deferred effect. With staged writes the mirror is always one flush behind props, and DbDemo re-creates the props.initial object on every dragVersion bump (spread at DbDemo.tsx:124), so the reset fires on every drag. Consider deriving the form values (createMemo over props) or remounting TaskForm keyed by selectedId instead of the effect-driven reset.

All five .tsx files in this batch begin with // @ts-nocheck, so none of the removed-export or JSX-namespace breakage (onMount, on, JSX from solid-js) will be caught by tsc during the migration. Remove the pragmas at least for the duration of the port.

audits.summary: 24 sites across 6 files. Mechanical work is small: 3 import lines (DbDemo onMount->onSettled+flush, TaskForm drop `on`, Modal `import type { JSX } from '@solidjs/web'`), one onMount->onSettled, one createEffect(on(...)) split, one untrack around a top-level props read, and four functional-updater rewrites in TaskForm. ResourceManager.tsx, BlockedManager.tsx and api.ts need no code changes at all. The risk is concentrated in DbDemo's drag pipeline: onDateChange is invoked synchronously from useDrag.handleMouseUp AFTER that handler drained the final pending move (which stages _bar writes), so every `taskStore.tasks[id]._bar` read at line 196 is one drag-frame stale — the PATCH loses the last frame and dependents that only moved on that frame are skipped entirely; worse, the post-await re-snapshot at line 239-242 reads the committed value, so lastX/lastWidth desync from dbState and the error compounds per drag. Fix with flush() at the top of onDateChange plus capturing bar.x/width into the patches array. Same class of problem at refetch's queueMicrotask(snapshotChartX) (line 100), which assumed a single microtask was enough for the Gantt's effect-driven re-layout. Two non-obvious traps: (1) the naive `onSettled(() => refetch('Loaded'))` THROWS in dev because the arrow returns a Promise and trackedEffect rejects non-function returns (@solidjs/signals dev.js:6283) — wrap in a block; (2) the onReady callback at line 364 fires from Gantt's onMount->onSettled (children-forbidden), so it must never create primitives — it currently only schedules a timer, which is legal. SMA found 3 of these 24 sites (DbDemo:111, TaskForm:231, TaskForm:232 — all confirmed) and missed Modal.tsx's JSX import, every import line, all four setter shims, the top-level props read, and all seven sync hazards. topLevelReadCount=1 (TaskForm.tsx:200).

syncHazards.description: WRITE: setSelectedIds(...) executed from Gantt.tsx:184-188's effect COMPUTE (wrapped in untrack, which does not clear the owner). READ: selectedIds() in JSX at 131-132. In rc.6 dev the write throws REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE before any read happens; in prod the write is staged and the badge updates only after the microtask flush, so any same-tick readback of selectedIds() is stale.

Compute must return a plain array (not the Set behind a store proxy) so apply never triggers STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED; drop untrack. Demo file needs no change.

syncHazards.description: WRITE then READ of the same signal in one expression: setCriticalPath(!criticalPath()) reads the committed value to compute the next one. Under deferred writes, a second toggle dispatched in the same synchronous tick (test harness, programmatic .click(), a synthetic double event) reads the pre-flush value and cancels the first write.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: setCriticalPath((v) => !v) — dev.js setSignal applies updater functions to the staged `_pendingValue`, so chained toggles compose correctly. In tests, call flush() after the click before asserting the button label/props.options.criticalPath.

syncHazards.description: WRITE: setApi(a) at line 197 fires from Gantt's onSettled (ex-onMount) and is STAGED. READ: api() at 101/109/119 inside the click handlers. A click (or programmatic click in a test) that lands in the same tick as mount, before the flush, sees null and the handler silently `return`s with no user feedback.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: In tests, flush() after render before clicking. In the demo, either disable the buttons off `api()` (`disabled={!api()}`) so the dead window is visible, or set a status message in the early-return branch instead of a bare `return`.

syncHazards.description: READ-after-WRITE across components: a.exportSvgBlob() reads taskStore.tasks (store proxy) and relationships() synchronously via Gantt's buildExportInput. If any staged store/signal write is still un-flushed when the export is invoked programmatically (e.g. from a script right after a data change, or immediately after a drag commit), the exported SVG serializes the previously committed geometry.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Call flush() (exported from 'solid-js') at the top of exportSvg/exportSvgBlob/exportPng in Gantt.tsx, or from the demo handler before invoking the API, so exports always serialize settled state. Real user clicks are already past a flush; this only bites programmatic/test callers.

The status DOM update cannot flush until after that blocking SVG build, so the 'Rasterizing' state is even less likely to paint than in 1.x.

syncHazards.description: Same deferred round-trip for the controlled <select value={filterPreset()}> / onChange pair; select.value remains a prop in 2.0, but the write-back and the downstream row re-filter (Gantt effectiveTasks -> runSetup) now land after the flush rather than during the change event.

structuralConcerns: Both selection demos (BoxSelectDemo:141, MultiSelectDemo:123) are blocked on Gantt.tsx:184-188: a single-arg createEffect that calls props.onSelectionChange inside untrack. Any consumer callback that writes a signal throws REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE in rc.6 dev (confirmed in @solidjs/signals dist/dev.js setSignal — the guard exempts only CONFIG_OWNED_WRITE signals and CONFIG_CHILDREN_FORBIDDEN contexts, and untrack leaves `context` set). This is a public-API contract change, not a local rewrite: every callback prop Gantt invokes from an effect must move to the apply phase, and the prop docs (Gantt.tsx:124-125) should state that callbacks run untracked/unowned after the flush.

ExportDemo's imperative bridge depends on Gantt.tsx:234 onMount(() => props.onReady?.(api)) becoming onSettled. onSettled is children-forbidden: any consumer that creates a primitive in its onReady callback (or in a helper the callback invokes) throws, and onCleanup inside throws CLEANUP_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE. Either document 'onReady: writes allowed, primitive creation forbidden' on GanttAPI, or fire onReady from an effect apply / queueMicrotask so consumer callbacks run in a fully unowned scope with no restrictions.

CriticalPathDemo's inline `options={{ ..., criticalPath: criticalPath() }}` (line 135) makes the entire options prop a rebuilt-per-read getter, which drives Gantt.tsx:306-309 (ganttConfig.updateOptions inside an effect compute — a store write that throws in 2.0) and Gantt.tsx:288-302 (runSetup -> setRelationships/setLegacyResources inside an effect compute). Per-key getters in the demo shrink the invalidation surface, but the toggle only works after those Gantt effects are split into compute/apply. FilterSearchDemo already uses the correct getter shape and therefore only trips the same Gantt effects via search/filter changes.

Out-of-batch but required to run these five demos: src/entries/{box-select,multi-select,export,filter-search,critical-path}.tsx each do `import { render } from 'solid-js/web'` -> '@solidjs/web'; tsconfig jsxImportSource must become '@solidjs/web'; vite-plugin-solid must be swapped for @solidjs/vite-plugin@3.0.0-next.35.

All five files open with `// @ts-nocheck`, so none of the 2.0 type-level breakages (JSX namespace moving to '@solidjs/web', Setter/StoreSetter signatures, removed solid-js exports) are visible to tsc. The migration should strip ts-nocheck per file as each is converted, otherwise these demos will only fail at runtime in the browser.

None of the five files import anything that moved: each imports only `createSignal` from 'solid-js' (plus a type-only import of GanttAPI in ExportDemo). There are no onMount/onCleanup/createEffect/createMemo/createComputed/batch/on/produce/unwrap/Index/Suspense/ErrorBoundary/classList/ref/use:/context sites in this batch — every breakage here is inherited through the Gantt props surface (callback ownership + deferred writes) rather than through local API renames.
audits.summary: Five demo files, 827 lines, mostly static task fixtures. No import changes are needed anywhere in this batch (each file imports only createSignal from 'solid-js'); no onMount/onCleanup/createEffect/createMemo/batch/on/produce/unwrap/Index/Show-callback/context/classList/ref/use:/attr: sites exist locally, and topLevelReadCount is 0 (every accessor read sits in JSX or an event handler). The real breakage is inherited through the Gantt props surface: (1) BoxSelectDemo:141 and MultiSelectDemo:123 pass setSelectedIds into onSelectionChange, which Gantt.tsx:184-188 invokes from an effect COMPUTE under untrack — a hard REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE throw in rc.6 dev (verified against dist/dev.js setSignal), fixable only by splitting that effect so the callback runs in apply; (2) ExportDemo:197's onReady write is legal because Gantt.tsx:234's onMount becomes onSettled, a children-forbidden scope that permits writes but forbids primitive creation and onCleanup — a new, undocumented contract for the GanttAPI bridge; (3) CriticalPathDemo:135 embeds a bare accessor call in the options object literal, making the whole prop a rebuilt getter that amplifies Gantt's illegal in-compute store writes (ganttConfig.updateOptions, runSetup) — rewrite to a per-key getter like FilterSearchDemo:189-194; (4) CriticalPathDemo:112 is a committed-value read-modify-write toggle that must become setCriticalPath(v => !v); (5) FilterSearchDemo:105 should become a createMemo so props.options.filter stops minting a new predicate identity per read. Eight sync hazards, two high (the selection callbacks). The SMA report lists zero sites for all five of these files, so every finding here is additional. Total 13 sites, effort S, mechanical except for the two structural Gantt-side dependencies.

syncHazards.description: Re-entrancy guard `if (dragState() !== 'idle') return;` reads a signal that startDrag itself writes at L218 (`setDragState(state)`). Under deferred writes the write is staged, so a second startDrag call in the SAME task (two mousedown handlers on nested elements where stopPropagation is missing, or a synthetic double-dispatch) reads the committed 'idle' and starts a second drag: duplicate document mousemove/mouseup listeners are registered (L224-225) and only one set is removed on mouseup, leaking a listener and double-firing onDragMove. index-test drives this via TestBarWithDrag L1451 and TestBarCombined L1550/1564/1569/1574.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Track drag activity with a plain closure boolean that is not subject to deferred commit: `let active = false;` set/cleared alongside setDragState, and use `if (active) return;` as the guard; keep the signal purely for rendering.

syncHazards.description: startTest reads `running()` as a toggle guard (`if (running()) { stopTest(); return; }`) and then writes `setRunning(true)` at L1952. The write is staged until the microtask flush, so any second invocation of startTest inside the same task (double click dispatch, programmatic call, or a stopTest()/startTest() pair in one handler) still sees running()===false and starts a second setInterval (L1963) and a second RAF loop, orphaning the previous intervalId/scrollAnimId — the onCleanup at L1995 only clears the latest one.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Keep a non-reactive `let isRunning = false;` as the source of truth for the guard and mirror it into the signal for rendering, or wrap the toggle in flush(() => { ... }) so the read after the write sees the new value.

syncHazards.description: Inside the setOffset updater, `direction()` is read (L1965) and `setDirection(-1/1)` is written (L1969/L1972) in the same synchronous updater. The read returns the committed value, so if two setOffset calls ever land in one tick (e.g. the interval and a scroll-driven update coincide, or UPDATE_INTERVAL is lowered below the flush granularity) both updaters compute with the pre-bounce direction and the bounce is applied twice / offset overshoots. Writing a second signal from inside another signal's updater also re-enters the notify path.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Restructure to compute first and write once: `const dir = direction(); let next = offset() + dir * SCROLL_STEP; if (next >= max) { setDirection(-1); next = max; } else if (next <= 0) { setDirection(1); next = 0; } setOffset(next);` — or make `direction` a plain closure variable since it is never rendered.

syncHazards.description: autoScroll reads `direction()` at L1932 and then stages `setDirection(-1)` / `setDirection(1)` at L1935/L1938 within the same RAF frame. It happens to be safe today because the bounce also clamps the local `currentScroll`, so the stale direction on the next read is never observed — but the pattern (write direction, keep scrolling from a signal read) breaks the moment the clamp is removed or two autoScroll frames run before a flush.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Demote `direction` to a plain closure variable (it is not rendered anywhere), or read it once into a local at the top of autoScroll and drive the bounce entirely from locals.

structuralConcerns: The harness's premise changes under 2.0. Its whole purpose is timing <Index> DOM-node recycling; <For keyed={false}> is a different reconciler (patch-driver / driveList in @solidjs/web) AND writes are deferred to a microtask flush, so the DOM update caused by setOffset in the interval callback (L1964) no longer happens inside that callback's task. createRAF's frame-to-frame measurement (L1879) therefore attributes the render to a different frame than in 1.x. All recorded baselines must be re-measured, and if synchronous-update semantics are wanted for comparability the interval body should be wrapped in flush(() => setOffset(...)).

The 'force memo evaluation' probes at L848, L903 and L974 (variants V7d/V7e/V7f) are meaningless in 2.0: createMemo computes eagerly on creation, so nothing is being forced, and each probe additionally emits a dev STRICT_READ warning 340x per frame (once per bar instance), which will itself dominate the profile in dev builds. These three variants need redesign or deletion rather than a mechanical rewrite.

All 20 variant components normalize their row prop with `typeof props.taskId === 'function' ? props.taskId() : props.taskId` (and `props.task` for the directTask family) purely because <Index> passed an accessor. <For keyed={false}> passes exactly the same accessor, so the shim keeps working, but the migration is the right moment to type these props as Accessor<T> and drop the runtime typeof branch from 20 call sites.

Dev-mode diagnostics volume: with 340 bars rendered per frame, every per-component STRICT_READ (L1283/1284 in TestBarWithContext, L1505 in TestBarCombined, plus the three void probes) fires per instance per re-create. Fix these before doing any perf comparison against 1.9 numbers, otherwise the 2.0 results are diagnostics-bound.

audits.summary: index-test.tsx is a 2360-line standalone perf harness (20 bar variants + one demo shell) whose required 2.0 changes are almost entirely mechanical and concentrated in the last 70 lines: 3 import lines (solid-js/web -> @solidjs/web; solid-js/store -> solid-js; drop the removed-but-unused onMount and the removed Index), 4 <Index> -> <For keyed={false}> sites at L2298/2307/2316/2325 (callback shape is already (accessor, number) so no callback edits), and <TestEventsContext.Provider> -> <TestEventsContext> at L2343 plus its closing tag at L2357 (which the advisory report omits). There are no store writes, no path setters, no produce/unwrap/reconcile, no batch, no on(), no createComputed, no createResource, no classList/use:/on:/attr:, no ref callbacks, and no 2-or-3-arg createMemo anywhere in the file - I checked all 90 createMemo calls with a paren-matching scan and every one is single-argument, so the batch note about '3-arg createMemo calls' does not hold for this file. Every setter call lives in an event handler, setInterval or requestAnimationFrame callback, so nothing trips REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE; the onCleanup at L1995 sits directly in a component body and stays legal (disputing the advisory report's 'migrate to returned cleanup' item, since there is no enclosing effect/onSettled). Gantt.tsx:235 is `onMount(() => props.onReady?.(api))`; under rc.6 that becomes onSettled, and onSettled called from an owned scope routes through createTrackedEffect (verified @solidjs/signals dist/dev.js:7217-7220 `createTrackedEffect(() => untrack(callback), { name: 'onSettled' })`), which validates the callback's return at dev.js:6282-6287: `if (cleanup !== undefined && typeof cleanup !== 'function') throw new Error("onSettled callback returned an invalid cleanup value...")`. ExportDemo's handler is the concise arrow `(a) => setApi(a)`; Setter<T> returns the new value (types signals.d.ts:60-65, and dev.js setSignal ends `return v` / `if (!valueChanged) return v`), so `props.onReady?.(api)` returns the GanttAPI object, the outer arrow returns it, and the mount throws in dev. The demo-features audit examined this exact line and concluded 'This demo is currently compliant; the constraint is new and load-bearing' — it checked the write guard (correctly: onSettled is CONFIG_CHILDREN_FORBIDDEN so the write is exempt) but not the return-value validation.

SAME RETURN-VALUE TRAP ON THE APPLY PHASE, and it is introduced BY the audit's own prescribed fix. createEffect's apply return is validated identically (dev.js:6232-6241: `const nextCleanup = node._effectFn(node._value, node._prevValue); if (nextCleanup !== undefined && typeof nextCleanup !== 'function') throw new Error("effect callback returned an invalid cleanup value...")`). The demo-features fix for Gantt.tsx:184-188 is `createEffect(() => [...ids], (ids) => props.onSelectionChange?.(new Set(ids)))` — a concise-arrow apply. This demo's handler is itself a concise arrow `(set) => setSelectedIds(Array.from(set).sort())`, so it returns the sorted string[] (Setter returns the new value), which propagates out of `props.onSelectionChange?.(...)`, out of the apply, and throws. Every reviewer treated the write guard as the only hazard on this line; the return value survives the write-guard fix and turns a working demo into a hard dev throw.

disputed.reason: WRONG PREMISE, HIGHEST-SEVERITY FINDING IN THAT BATCH. demo-perf-profiler files a `severity: high` sync hazard claiming that because onSettled is a tracked effect, `startFpsCounter()`'s internal `running()` read subscribes the onSettled bundle to createRAF's signal, `setRunning(true)` dirties it, and the whole body re-runs so `loadTasks()` fires twice, 'polluting the benchmark numbers'. Two independent verifications refute it. (1) onSettled explicitly untracks its callback: @solidjs/signals dist/dev.js:7217-7220 is `createTrackedEffect(() => untrack(callback), { name: 'onSettled' })`, and dist/types/signals.d.ts:645-646 states 'Reactive reads inside the callback are *not* tracked — to react to subsequent settles, register a new onSettled each time.' No subscription is created, so no re-run. (2) @solid-primitives/raf 4.0.0-next.2 (the version the same audit prescribes) creates its latch as `createSignal(false, { ownedWrite: true })` (dist/index.js), so even the write-guard half of the concern is moot. The prescribed rewrite `onSettled(() => { untrack(() => { loadTasks(); startFpsCounter(); }); })` is therefore redundant. Only the audit's secondary sub-claim survives, at low severity: start()'s `if (running()) return; setRunning(true)` guard reads committed state, so two start() calls in one tick would launch two RAF loops.

Same wrong premise, propagated into a forward-looking warning. Note (e) on this site asserts 'onSettled is a TRACKED effect, and the body registers zero dependencies ... so it runs once — but note the body writes viewportWidth, so adding any reactive read to the body later would create a self-triggering loop.' The self-triggering loop cannot happen: the callback is wrapped in an unlabeled untrack (dev.js:7220), so a reactive read added to the onSettled body later still creates no subscription and still cannot re-arm the effect. The correct forward-looking warning is the opposite one — a read added to an onSettled body silently will NOT react, so anyone expecting re-run-on-change must register a fresh onSettled. (The demo-experiments audit repeats the same 'TRACKED effect' premise at GanttExperiments.tsx:964 and the FACTS brief item 3 states it too; the demo-showcase audit is the only one that got this right, and its stated dispute with the brief is correct.)

MEDIUM HAZARD LIKELY NOT REAL — the microtask ordering works out. demo-db claims 'a single queued microtask is no longer a guarantee that those effect-phase store writes have committed', so snapshotChartX can read the OLD layout. But `setBundle(data)` at line 93 runs first and its write calls schedule(), which is literally `if (scheduled) return; scheduled = true; if (!syncDepth && !globalQueue._running && !projectionWriteActive) queueMicrotask(flush)` (dev.js:1601-1609). refetch is an async continuation, so none of those bail-outs apply and the flush microtask is enqueued at line 93 — strictly BEFORE `queueMicrotask(snapshotChartX)` at line 100. Microtasks are FIFO, so flush() runs first, and per the rc.6 contract writes made during the effect phase 'are queued into the same flush's continuation — dependent memos and effects update before the flush returns' (signals.d.ts:652-656). I also confirmed the producer is not deferred behind rAF/timers: Gantt.tsx:290-304 re-runs runSetup from a plain createEffect body, so the _bar writes land inside that same flush. Conclusion: snapshotChartX sees committed positions. The audit's suggested `queueMicrotask(() => { flush(); snapshotChartX(); })` is harmless but unnecessary. (This does NOT weaken the batch's real hazard at DbDemo:196 — that one is a same-synchronous-task read-after-write inside the mouseup stack and is correctly diagnosed.)

Overstated. demo-features files a medium hazard that 'a click (or programmatic click in a test) that lands in the same tick as mount, before the flush, sees null'. @solidjs/web render() ends with an explicit `flush()` inside its try block (dist/dev.js:377-402: createRoot(...) { insert(..., { schedule: true }) }; flush();), and onSettled runs during that flush with its write processed in the same flush's continuation. So by the time `render(() => <ExportDemo />, root)` returns, api() is already committed — there is no observable null window for either a real user click or a test that clicks after render(). What remains is only the ordinary case where onReady never fires (Gantt failed to mount), which is a pre-existing condition, not a deferred-write regression. Note this line has a genuinely worse problem the same audit missed: the concise-arrow return value (see 'missed', ExportDemo.tsx:197).

Minor factual overreach. The note says to use a block body because '2.0 reserves ref-callback return values'. @solidjs/web types/jsx.d.ts:243-244 declares `type RefCallback<T> = (el: T) => void; type Ref<T> = T | RefCallback<T> | undefined | Ref<T>[]` — the return is typed void, and there is no runtime consumption of a ref callback's return value anywhere in the rc.6 client build (unlike onSettled/createEffect-apply, which do validate it). The block-body rewrite is still the right edit, but the reason is a TypeScript excess-return error once @ts-nocheck comes off, not a reserved runtime slot. Getting this right matters because the audits then under-weight the places where a returned value genuinely throws.

crossCutting: RETURN-VALUE VALIDATION IS A NEW, UNNAMED HAZARD CLASS AND NO AUDIT NAMES IT. rc.6 validates the return of two callback shapes: onSettled/createTrackedEffect (dev.js:6282-6287) and createEffect's apply phase (dev.js:6232-6241), both throwing 'callback returned an invalid cleanup value. Return a cleanup function or undefined.' Meanwhile Setter<T> still RETURNS the new value (signals.d.ts:60-65; setSignal ends `return v`). So every concise arrow of the shape `() => setX(...)`, `(v) => setX(v)`, or `() => somethingAsync()` becomes a dev throw the moment it lands in an onSettled body or an effect apply. In this area that is at least four live sites — DbDemo.tsx:111 (async, the one audit that caught it), ExportDemo.tsx:197, BoxSelectDemo.tsx:141, MultiSelectDemo.tsx:123 — plus every split-effect rewrite the audits propose with a concise apply (demo-features' Gantt.tsx:184-188 fix, demo-components' ConstraintDemo:662 fix, demo-showcase's updateTaskA/updateTaskB mirrors). File it as one repo rule: any callback that crosses a component boundary or is handed to createEffect/onSettled gets a block body, full stop. It is mechanical, greppable (`=> set[A-Z]`, `=> props\.on[A-Z]`), and invisible to tsc while @ts-nocheck stands.

onSettled IS NOT TRACKED, AND THE BRIEF SAYS IT IS. FACTS item 3 calls onSettled 'a children-forbidden tracked effect'; four of the eight audits built reasoning on that (demo-perf-profiler's only high-severity hazard, demo-perf-isolate's L1758 note (e), demo-experiments' L964 note, demo-components' correct-but-differently-argued ArrowDemo:350 note). The implementation is `createTrackedEffect(() => untrack(callback), { name: 'onSettled' })` (dev.js:7220) and the doc is explicit: 'Reactive reads inside the callback are *not* tracked — to react to subsequent settles, register a new onSettled each time' (signals.d.ts:645-646). Correct the brief once rather than per batch: onSettled never re-runs, never subscribes, and never emits STRICT_READ; the real trap is the opposite (a read placed there is silently inert).

THE 'running()/recording() AS ITS OWN LATCH' PATTERN IS ONE ISSUE, NOT FIVE. Every perf harness in this area reimplements a start/stop toggle whose guard reads the signal the same function writes: GanttExperiments.tsx:898 (flagged), index-test.tsx:1947 (flagged), GanttMinimalTest.tsx:340 (missed), GanttPerfDemo.tsx:110/161/211 (missed), GanttProfiler.tsx:83/87 (flagged low), plus the same shape inside @solid-primitives/raf's own start() and src/hooks/useDrag.ts:196. Under deferred writes all seven read committed state. One shared fix — a plain closure boolean as the latch, the signal kept purely as a render mirror — resolves the whole set, and it is cheaper than the flush()-based fixes several audits propose.

THE onMount + ResizeObserver/setTimeout/RAF + onCleanup BODY IS COPY-PASTED FIVE TIMES. GanttMinimalTest.tsx:417/439, GanttExperiments.tsx:964/978, GanttPerfIsolate.tsx:1758/1769, GanttPerfDemo.tsx:269/276/298, GanttProfiler.tsx:165/177 are near-identical: measure the container, observe resize, start a RAF/interval, register onCleanup. Every one needs the same three edits (onSettled, onCleanup -> a single returned disposer merging listener + timer + RAF handles) and three of them leak an uncancelled RAF today (GanttMinimalTest:468, GanttPerfIsolate:1806, GanttExperiments' stress loop). This should be one `onSettled`-based viewport/FPS helper in the demo tree, migrated once, not five hand-rolled conversions with five chances to drop a clearTimeout.

'WRITE A CONFIG SIGNAL/STORE, THEN SYNCHRONOUSLY RE-READ IT TO MIRROR INTO taskStore' IS ONE ARCHITECTURAL DEFECT SPREAD ACROSS THREE FILES. ShowcaseDemo hazards #1-#7 (input handler -> setTaskConfig -> updateTaskA re-reads taskConfig), ConstraintDemo hazard #1 (setSelectedScenario -> updateTasks re-reads the allTasks memo), and DbDemo hazards #1/#2 (drag -> _bar re-read from the live store proxy) are filed as three unrelated hazard sets across three batches. They are the same shape and have the same fix: derive the mirror with a split createEffect (compute reads the config into a PLAIN object, apply writes the store) instead of pairing a write with an imperative re-read. Doing it once removes ~10 of the area's high-severity hazards; patching each with flush() leaves the shape in place to be re-introduced by the next handler.

createMemo's 1.x INITIAL VALUE HAS A REAL rc.6 SUCCESSOR AND NO AUDIT MENTIONS IT. MemoOptions now carries `loadingValue?: T` — 'Commit #0: a committed value the memo is born with ... The loading value is also the compute's first prev' (signals.d.ts:200-224), with a dedicated overload `createMemo<T>(compute, options: MemoOptions<T> & { loadingValue: T })` (signals.d.ts:295-297). Both the SMA guidance and the demo-perf-profiler rewrite for benchmarks/profiler/instrumentation/memoTracker.js:136 treat the initial value as simply deleted (drop the `undefined`, move options into slot 2) and recommend a default parameter on the compute. That is right for this call, but the migration playbook for the whole repo should record loadingValue as the first-class option, since createTrackedMemo is a public profiling API whose callers may have relied on an initial value.

SCOPE-PARTITION GAP: src/demo/CustomColumnsDemo.tsx belongs to this area, is mounted by an in-scope entry (src/entries/custom-columns.tsx:6), and appears in NO batch's file list. I read it: 158 lines, zero solid-js imports, no For/Show/Index/store/lifecycle, one plain `render: (task) =>
…
` column callback that creates no primitives — so there are no migration sites, but it does contain JSX and therefore depends on the tsconfig jsxImportSource flip to '@solidjs/web' like every other file here. TOOLING VERIFIED FROM THE TARBALLS, TWO AUDIT CAVEATS CAN BE CLOSED. @solid-primitives/raf 4.0.0-next.2 still returns `[running, start, stop]` and now creates its latch with `createSignal(false, { ownedWrite: true })`, so the write-guard worry raised for GanttPerfDemo.tsx:64 and index-test.tsx:1875 is moot and the existing tuple destructures need no change; it imports `isServer` from '@solidjs/web' and `noop` from @solid-primitives/utils, confirming both peer bumps are mandatory. @solidjs/web render() ends with an explicit flush() and wraps the mount in enforceLoadingBoundary(true) (dist/dev.js:377-402), which confirms the entries batch's ASYNC_OUTSIDE_LOADING_BOUNDARY note and closes the 'does the mount still attach synchronously' question for all 20 entries. SMA coverage is complete for this area: all 64 in-scope SMA lines are reproduced by some audit, and I found no SMA site that was dropped.
critic.summary:
Ran independent greps for every FACTS pattern across all 47 in-scope files and reconciled hit-by-hit against the eight audits, then verified the sharp claims against the rc.6 tarballs (@solidjs/signals dist/dev.js + types, @solidjs/web types/jsx.d.ts + dist/dev.js, @solid-primitives/raf 4.0.0-next.2). SMA coverage is complete — all 64 in-scope sma-report lines are accounted for by some audit, none dropped — and the audits' import/Index/onMount/produce/batch/path-setter inventories are accurate (I re-counted ShowcaseDemo's 38 store setters, GanttExperiments' two options-shaped 2-arg memos, GanttPerfIsolate's 8 useGanttEvents sites and 6 top-level reads, index-test's 7 top-level reads and 4 Index sites, and confirmed zero classList/use:/on:/attr:/bool:/@once/createComputed/createResource/Suspense/Portal/createRoot/destructured-props anywhere in the area).

The biggest gap is a hazard class nobody named: rc.6 validates the RETURN VALUE of onSettled callbacks (dev.js:6282-6287, reached via `createTrackedEffect(() => untrack(callback))` at 7220) and of createEffect's apply phase (dev.js:6232-6241), throwing on any non-undefined, non-function return — while Setter<T> still returns the new value. That turns four in-scope concise arrows into dev throws (ExportDemo:197 onReady, BoxSelectDemo:141 and MultiSelectDemo:123 onSelectionChange, plus the already-caught DbDemo:111), and it silently breaks the split-effect rewrites that demo-features, demo-components and demo-showcase prescribe. I also found four missed read-then-write latches of a class other batches did flag (GanttMinimalTest:340, GanttPerfDemo:110/161/211) and one dead import (ShowcaseDemo:6 Show).

Five disputes, two of them consequential. demo-perf-profiler's only high-severity finding — that GanttPerfDemo:334's onSettled body re-subscribes through createRAF and fires loadTasks twice — is refuted twice over: onSettled untracks its callback (signals.d.ts:645-646) and raf 4.0.0-next.2 marks its latch `ownedWrite: true`. The same 'onSettled is tracked' premise (which the FACTS brief itself asserts, and which only the demo-showcase audit challenged) also invalidates a forward-looking warning at GanttPerfIsolate:1758. demo-db's DbDemo:100 queueMicrotask hazard does not survive scheduler ordering — setBundle's schedule() enqueues the flush microtask before queueMicrotask(snapshotChartX), and Gantt's runSetup writes land inside that flush — and demo-features' ExportDemo:101 null-api window is closed by render()'s tail flush(). Cross-cutting, the area has one architectural defect (write-config-then-re-read-to-mirror) filed as three separate hazard sets, one lifecycle body copy-pasted five times, one latch pattern repeated seven times, and one unaudited file (CustomColumnsDemo.tsx) that is in src/demo but in no batch's scope list.

syncHazards.description: test.environment:'node' puts @solidjs/vite-plugin into its SERVER posture: the plugin skips injecting the 'browser' condition and force-inlines solid-js/@solidjs/web (test.server.deps.inline=[/solid-js/,/@solidjs[+/]web/]) so the SERVER build resolves - a build with no subscription graph. Every reactive assertion in tests/taskStore.test.ts (createRoot + createMemo over store.tasks[id]._bar.x, lines 87-360) and tests/selectionStore.test.ts (lines 66-95) would write and then read a memo that never recomputed. Combined with 2.0's deferred writes (the read is stale even on the client build without a flush), the suite can go green while asserting nothing, or fail in a way that looks like a store bug.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Drop `environment: 'node'` and `resolve.conditions` entirely, add a jsdom devDependency, and let the plugin apply its client posture (jsdom + solid/development/browser conditions). Then add `flush()` after every write before an assertion. If a node environment is genuinely required, you must keep an explicit `resolve.conditions: ['solid','development','browser']` and verify at runtime that `import('solid-js')` resolves dist/dev.js, not dist/server.js.

syncHazards.description: Documented house pattern 'Gantt Y-sync effect: wrap position updates in untrack() to avoid feedback loop'. In 2.0 untrack() disables tracking but does NOT clear the owner, so a store write executed inside a createEffect compute callback throws REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE in dev even when wrapped. Any contributor following this doc writes code that throws on first render; worse, the pattern's intent (write derived positions back into the store from an effect) is exactly the write-then-read shape that deferred writes break, because the same effect then re-reads the positions it just staged.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Rewrite the guidance (and src/components/Gantt.tsx) as a split effect: createEffect(compute, apply) where compute reads plain values (numbers, not store proxies) and returns them, and apply performs the setStore(draft => ...) write. The apply callback runs from the scheduler with no owner, so it may write legally, and it is untracked by construction - the untrack() wrapper becomes unnecessary.

syncHazards.description: The documented drag-persistence algorithm (steps 1-5, lines 136-145; implemented in src/demo/DbDemo.tsx) writes bar positions through the chart's store during drag and then, on the onDateChange callback, WALKS THE SAME STORE reading `_bar.x`/`_bar.width` to diff them against a snapshot. If onDateChange is emitted in the same synchronous tick as the store write (drag-end handler, or a constraint cascade applying updates), every read returns the previously committed value, so Δx and Δwidth compute as 0 and no PATCH is sent - the drag silently fails to persist. The move/resize disambiguation table (lines 149-153) keys entirely off those deltas, so a partially-flushed read could also mis-classify a resize as a move.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Await the flush before diffing: make the onDateChange handler `async (id, dates) => { await flush(); ...walk store... }` (or queueMicrotask), or - better - have the chart pass the new geometry to the callback explicitly so the demo never re-reads the store it just wrote. Update both this doc and CLAUDE.md:265-269.

syncHazards.description: Same hazard restated as repo guidance: 'it snapshots each bar's _bar.x and _bar.width, computes per-task pixel deltas after drag, and PATCHes in parallel'. As written it instructs future contributors to read store geometry immediately after the chart mutated it. Under deferred writes 'after drag' is not 'after commit'.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Amend the bullet to state that the delta walk must run after the microtask flush, and add a repo-wide rule near the top of CLAUDE.md: 'never read back a value you just wrote in the same tick - read the draft inside the setter, pass the value explicitly, or flush()'.

syncHazards.description: The documented constraint resolution flow is a write-then-read chain: resolveConstraints() reads committed geometry through context.getBarPosition (lines 596-604), the caller then calls taskStore.updateBarPosition() for the dragged task, then applies cascadeUpdates to successors, and finally expects arrow paths to recalculate. If any of those steps re-enters resolveConstraints or recomputes cascade geometry in the same tick, it plans against pre-write positions; multi-step relaxation across ticks can also converge on the wrong answer because 'current position (with any pending update)' (line 631) is no longer visible through a store read.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Apply the dragged position and every cascade update inside ONE setStore(draft => { ... }) callback - the draft reflects staged state, so the relaxation loop can read its own pending updates - and keep resolveConstraints pure over an explicitly passed position map rather than over live store reads. Document the flush boundary in the diagram.

syncHazards.description: The 'Target (functional)' drag template writes taskStore.updateBarPosition(taskId, { x: newX }) inside a RAF-driven onDragMove. The write itself is legal (event/RAF scope, no owner), but any code later in the same handler that re-reads the bar position - constraint clamping, arrow endpoints, snap feedback - sees the previous frame's value, producing a one-frame lag or an oscillation during fast drags.
syncHazards.suggestedFix: Annotate the template: compute newX once and pass it to every consumer in the handler; never re-read taskStore for a value written in the same frame. If a helper genuinely needs the post-write state, do the work inside the setter's draft callback.

structuralConcerns: VITEST POSTURE IS THE ONE REAL DECISION IN THIS BATCH. Verified in @solidjs/vite-plugin@3.0.0-next.35 dist: serverTestPosture is set when test.environment is 'node' or 'edge-runtime'; configEnvironment then injects ['solid', 'development'] but NOT 'browser', and config() force-inlines solid-js/@solidjs/web so the server build resolves end to end. solid-js@2.0.0-rc.6's exports map is ordered worker > browser > deno > node > development, so the FIRST matching condition key wins - which is why the repo's hand-written resolve.conditions:['development','browser'] would still (accidentally) select dist/dev.js. Recommendation: delete both `environment:'node'` and the `resolve` block, add jsdom, and let the plugin own it. That is the tested path, and no test in tests/ touches document/window today.

audits.summary: Tooling is a small, well-bounded change; the docs are the long tail. DEPENDENCIES (package.json): bump solid-js ^1.9.12 -> 2.0.0-rc.6 (L101) and ADD @solidjs/web 2.0.0-rc.6 (mandatory - the native compiler emits every JSX runtime import with moduleName '@solidjs/web', the plugin peer-requires it, and @solid-primitives/raf@4 imports isServer from it); replace vite-plugin-solid ^2.11.12 (L85) with @solidjs/vite-plugin 3.0.0-next.35; delete babel-preset-solid (L70, no babel config exists in the repo); bump @solid-primitives/raf ^2.3.4 -> 4.0.0-next.2 (L97, the only imported primitive: src/demo/GanttPerfDemo.tsx:3, src/entries/index-test.tsx:15); delete @solid-primitives/memo, resize-observer, scheduled, scroll (L96, L98-100 - repo-wide grep proves all four are unimported); add jsdom if you adopt the plugin's default test environment. VITE LIB (config/vite/solid.js): external L18 must become ['solid-js','@solidjs/web'] and the UMD globals map L22 must be re-keyed to '@solidjs/web' -> SolidJSWeb, or the DOM runtime gets bundled into dist and the UMD build emits a missing-global warning; a side benefit is that the store runtime (today imported from the un-externalized 'solid-js/store') becomes correctly external. TSCONFIG: jsxImportSource 'solid-js' -> '@solidjs/web' (L8; tsconfig.build.json inherits it). VITEST: the sharpest tooling hazard - `environment: 'node'` (L15) puts @solidjs/vite-plugin into its server posture, which resolves the server build with no subscription graph; recommended posture is to delete both `environment` and the hand-written `resolve.conditions` (L11), add jsdom, and let the plugin inject jsdom + solid/development/browser. ESLINT: no globals change is required at all. CI: .github/workflows/publish.yml pins node-version '18' but the plugin requires ^20.19||>=22.12 - a hard release-job break. DOCS: 40 sentences across CLAUDE.md, README.md and 7 doc files go wrong, headlined by README.md:106 ('useGanttStores() returns undefined outside a provider' - createContext<T>() with no default now THROWS ContextNotFoundError, so the documented graceful fallback dies), docs/PERFORMANCE.md:407 (which prescribes wrapping store WRITES in untrack() inside an effect - fatal under the 2.0 write guard), docs/MINIMAL_TEST.md:54/76 (<Index> -> <For keyed={false}>), ANALYSIS.md:110/300 (Index-based headers), and every createStore/solid-js-store reference. Six sync hazards, three of them high: the vitest server-build posture, the untrack-wrapped effect write, and the DbDemo drag-PATCH algorithm documented at docs/DATABASE.md:136-145 / CLAUDE.md:265-269 that writes bar geometry and then reads it back in the same tick to compute pixel deltas. Also note dist-demo/ is committed (9 tracked files carrying the 1.9 runtime) and is what the benchmark scripts serve, so it must be rebuilt with the migration. The SMA report lists nothing for any file in this batch.

It checked the wrong store. `src/stores/ganttConfigStore.ts` declares `expandedTasks: Set<string>` as a FIELD OF `GanttConfigState` (line 54), initialises it inside `createStore` (line 146: `expandedTasks: new Set(options.expandedTasks || [])`), and mutates it IN PLACE at lines 175, 189 and 199 via `setState('expandedTasks', produce((set: Set<string>) => { set.add(taskId) / set.delete(taskId) }))`. Under FACT 6 that is a triple break: Sets are not proxied in 2.0 so the in-place add/delete notifies nothing, `produce` no longer exists, and the `setState(path, ...)` form is gone. Subtask expand/collapse would silently stop re-rendering. Only the reassigning paths (lines 206/210, `setState('expandedTasks', new Set(...))`) survive semantically. This doc line is the canonical 'why createStore' explainer, so it is where the rule has to be written down.
missed.rewrite: Append to the paragraph: 'In 2.0 plain objects and user class instances are still proxied deeply, but built-in collections (Set/Map/Date) are NOT. A Set or Map held as a store field and mutated in place notifies nothing — you must reassign the property. This repo has exactly one such field: `ganttConfigStore`'s `expandedTasks`. Its in-place `produce(set => set.add(id))` mutations must become `setState(draft => { draft.expandedTasks = new Set(draft.expandedTasks).add(id) })` (or the field must move out of the store into a `createSignal<Set<string>>`, which is what taskStore.collapsedTasks, resourceStore.collapsedGroups and selectionStore.selectedIds already do).'

missed.description: `const bar = untrack(() => task._bar);` followed on line 422 by `if (bar && (bar.x + bar.width < sx - 200 || bar.x > ex + 200)) continue;`. The audit marks lines 405/406 and this sample as 'Keep (untrack around READS is still correct inside a memo)'. But the sample does not do what the surrounding prose claims (line 406: 'TaskLayer visibleTaskIds: Use untrack() for _bar access during X filtering'). `untrack` only wraps fetching the `_bar` CHILD PROXY; every subsequent property read — `bar.x`, `bar.width`, twice each — happens outside the untrack call and therefore still subscribes to `tasks[id]._bar.x` and `.width`. The README has no installation section at all (verified: no `npm install`, no `pnpm add`; the only pnpm lines are 138/139/153/154 and they are contributor instructions). It jumps straight from the tagline to a `jsx` fence at line 7. That was survivable on Solid 1.9 where `jsxImportSource: 'solid-js'` was the universal default; it is not survivable on 2.0. A consumer must now (a) install `solid-js@2.0.0-rc.6` AND `@solidjs/web@2.0.0-rc.6` themselves — both are externalized by config/vite/solid.js and @solidjs/web is not a transitive dep of solid-js (verified: solid-js's exports map is only ['.','./refresh','./package.json'] and @solidjs/web peers on solid-js, not the reverse) — and (b) set `"jsxImportSource": "@solidjs/web"` in their OWN tsconfig, because solid-js 2.0 ships no jsx-runtime and the `.d.ts` files emitted by tsconfig.build.json will reference @solidjs/web's JSX namespace. The audit's README:3 rewrite adds the peer versions but never mentions jsxImportSource, which is the setting that decides whether `<Gantt tasks={tasks} />` type-checks in the consumer's project at all.

disputed.reason: The rewrite note's Set-in-store survey reaches a false-negative conclusion. It writes: 'Any remaining Set/Map inside a store (e.g. collapsedTasks) needs auditing - tests/taskStore.test.ts:320 reads store.collapsedTasks().size, which is a signal-of-Set (fine), not a store-held Set.' That single data point is correct (I confirmed tests/taskStore.test.ts:320 is `createMemo(() => store.collapsedTasks().size)` over a signal) but it is presented as the resolution of the audit, and the actual store-held Set is in a different file the note never opens. src/stores/ganttConfigStore.ts:54 declares `expandedTasks: Set<string>` as a member of `GanttConfigState`, line 146 initialises it inside the `createStore` call, and lines 175/189/199 mutate it in place with `setState('expandedTasks', produce((set: Set<string>) => set.add/delete(taskId)))`. Under FACT 6 those mutations notify nothing in 2.0 (Sets are unproxied), and they additionally use two removed APIs (`produce`, the path-setter form). A reader who trusts this note will ship a subtask expand/collapse feature that silently stops re-rendering. The note should say the opposite of what it says: there IS exactly one store-held Set in the repo and it is the highest-severity silent break in the store layer.

The fallback advice is unsafe and contradicts the plugin's documented design. The site says: 'If you insist on keeping environment:"node", you MUST keep an explicit "browser" condition here or the tests go non-reactive.' The first half is mechanically true — I confirmed in @solidjs/vite-plugin@3.0.0-next.38 that configEnvironment does `config.resolve.conditions = ['solid', ...(replaceDev?['development']:[]), ...(isTestMode && !serverTestPosture ? ['browser'] : []), ...config.resolve.conditions]`, so a user-supplied 'browser' survives into the server posture and solid-js's exports map (worker > browser > deno > node > development) then still selects browser.development -> dist/dev.js. But the resulting configuration is a hybrid the plugin explicitly refuses to produce: in the SAME branch serverTestPosture also force-inlines the runtimes (`test.server.deps.inline = [/solid-js/, /@solidjs[+/]web/]`) with the stated goal of 'one server-build instance end to end (request-event storage included)', and the plugin's codegen selects SSR output for the same posture. Forcing 'browser' back in gives you client-build reactivity + server-posture codegen + inlining, with `isServer` false inside a `node` environment that has no DOM. That combination is untested upstream and will drift on any plugin bump. The honest fallback is not 'keep the browser condition' but 'do not mix postures in one config — use test.projects', which is what the plugin's own source comment prescribes ('Per-vitest-project posture ... Each vitest project resolves its own config').

The pin `"@solidjs/vite-plugin": "3.0.0-next.35"` is a version behind the compiler generation this migration targets, and next.38 is already fetched into the scratchpad the audit was working from. next.35 declares `"@solidjs/babel-plugin": "^2.0.0-rc.3"` and `"@solidjs/compiler": "^2.0.0-rc.3"`; next.38 declares `^2.0.0-rc.6` for both — matching the solid-js/@solidjs/web 2.0.0-rc.6 runtime the rest of the plan pins exactly. The caret ranges mean both would install rc.6 in a fresh lockfile, so this is not a correctness bug, but it makes the plugin's own floor inconsistent with the exact-pin policy the audit argues for two sites earlier ('Pin exact rc versions rather than ^ ranges: ^2.0.0-rc.6 admits rc.7+ whose semantics may move again'). next.38 also carries behavioural changes in exactly the area this batch decides — it adds `env.mode !== 'test'` guards around the diagnostics/HMR plugin branches (dist/esm/index.mjs:734, :2261) that next.35 lacks, i.e. next.35 will attempt to install the diagnostics bridge during `vitest run`. Recommend `3.0.0-next.38`; both versions carry identical peers (solid-js ^2.0.0-rc.0, @solidjs/web ^2.0.0-rc.0, vite ^8||^9) and identical engines (node ^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0), so the rest of the audit's reasoning is unaffected.

The rewrite tells consumers 'UMD consumers must supply the `SolidJS` and `SolidJSWeb` globals', and the config/vite/solid.js:22 site builds on the same premise. No such globals can be supplied. I unpacked both tarballs: solid-js@2.0.0-rc.6/dist contains dev.js, dev.cjs, solid.js, solid.cjs, server.js, server.cjs, refresh.* and @solidjs/web@2.0.0-rc.6/dist contains dev.js, dev.cjs, web.js, web.cjs, server.js, server.cjs — every one is ESM or CJS, and both packages' `unpkg`/`jsdelivr` fields point at ESM (`./dist/solid.js`, `./dist/web.js`). Neither ships an IIFE/global bundle, so a script-tag consumer has nothing to load that would define `window.SolidJS` or `window.SolidJSWeb`. Re-keying `output.globals` (the L22 site) is still necessary to stop rollup emitting a 'Missing global variable name' warning and to keep the build honest, but the README must not promise a consumer story that cannot be executed. The migration is the right moment to either drop `formats: ['es','umd']` down to `['es']` or add a separate non-externalized bundle — see the missed finding on config/vite/solid.js:14.

crossCutting: ONE STORE-SETTER IDIOM, NOT N DOC EDITS. `makeSetter<K extends keyof GanttConfigState>` (ganttConfigStore.ts:169, 'Builds a Setter<T>-compatible function that targets a single store path') is the shared shim behind every accessor/setter pair the docs describe as 'signals' — docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:398-431 (the whole config Signals table + API block), README.md:108, CLAUDE.md:97. It is built on `setState(key, value)`, the removed path-setter form, and typed as `Setter<T>`/`Setter<Set<string>>` (ganttConfigStore.ts:100). Rewriting that ONE helper to `(v) => setState(draft => { draft[key] = typeof v === 'function' ? v(draft[key]) : v })` preserves the public `Setter<T>` contract (the updater overload keeps working because the draft reflects staged state) and makes ~25 documented setters correct at once. File it as one issue, not as 21 table rows.

SET/MAP INVENTORY IS A FOUR-SITE PATTERN WITH EXACTLY ONE BROKEN MEMBER. The repo reaches for Set/Map for collapse/selection state in four places, and 2.0 splits them cleanly: SAFE (signal-of-Set, copy-on-write, survives untouched) = src/stores/taskStore.ts collapsedTasks, src/stores/resourceStore.ts:51 collapsedGroups, src/stores/selectionStore.ts:32 selectedIds (all three already do `setX(prev => new Set(prev))`); BROKEN (store-held Set mutated in place) = src/stores/ganttConfigStore.ts expandedTasks (declared L54, created inside createStore L146, mutated L175/189/199). Also adjacent: resourceStore.ts:62 `createMemo<Map<string,number>>` and docs/PERFORMANCE.md:350-351 `createMemo(() => { const index = new Map() ... })` are fine (a Map BUILT inside a memo, not held in a store). One issue should carry this whole table, because the docs that describe the pattern — docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:379, CLAUDE.md:101, docs/MINIMAL_TEST.md:129-148 — all need the same sentence and the reviewer needs the safe/broken split to avoid over-migrating the three healthy ones.

TEST RUNTIME POSTURE IS ONE ATOMIC CHANGE ACROSS THREE FILES PLUS A SUITE THE AUDIT NEVER OPENED. package.json (add jsdom devDependency — node_modules currently has neither jsdom nor happy-dom), vitest.config.ts (environment + resolve.conditions + projects), and tests/server/** (4 node-runtime suites: better-sqlite3 `new Database(':memory:')`, drizzle `migrate(...)` off the filesystem, Hono `app.fetch(new Request(...))`) must land together. The plugin's source settles the shape: `serverTestPosture = isTestMode && (test.environment === 'node' || 'edge-runtime')` is computed per resolved config and its comment reads 'Per-vitest-project posture: the client posture ... is right for DOM component tests but wrong for server-runtime unit tests ... Each vitest project resolves its own config.' vitest 4 `test.projects` is therefore the only shape that satisfies both halves; a flat config forces a wrong answer for one of them. Note also the plugin's warning that 'the worker pool is shared across the whole vitest workspace and imports externalized deps natively with --conditions derived from the ROOT config', so the root config should stay condition-free and let each project own its posture.

THE 1.9 PERFORMANCE CORPUS AND THE COMMITTED ARTIFACTS ARE ONE DELIVERABLE. ~10 result tables across docs/PERFORMANCE.md (13-20, 292-300, 385-393, 524-529), docs/DEMOS.md (121-126, 130-140, 202-208), docs/EXPERIMENTS.md (33-44) and benchmarks/traces/ANALYSIS.md (9-16, 178-254) were all measured on solid-js 1.9.12, AND the harness they measure is `dist-demo/` — 9 files tracked in git (verified: 3 examples/*.html + 6 hashed chunks; .gitignore ignores `dist/*` but not `dist-demo`) served by benchmarks/scripts/*.sh via `npx serve dist-demo -l 5174`. Re-baselining is therefore not 10 doc edits but one sequenced task: `pnpm build:demo` -> commit artifacts -> re-run the bench scripts -> date-stamp the old tables as 'solid-js 1.9.12' and append new ones. Additionally, the `<Index>` -> `<For keyed={false}>` conversions change the thing being measured, so the 'Index-based headers are 4-10% slower' finding (ANALYSIS.md:110, :300; DEMOS.md:76) is not merely unverified, it is testing a different implementation. Worth noting for the slot-pool cases specifically: rc.6 adds `<Repeat count={n} from={...}>` (verified in solid-js types/client/flow.d.ts), which is a closer match to DateHeadersOptimized's fixed-slot-pool idiom than `<For keyed={false}>` and should at least be benchmarked against it.

FILES OUTSIDE THIS BATCH'S LIST CARRY THE SAME GUIDANCE AND WILL DRIFT. (a) AGENTS.md (84 lines, root) is the non-Claude agent entry point and shares no content with CLAUDE.md — it will not receive the deferred-write rule the audit is adding to CLAUDE.md:7, so any agent that reads AGENTS.md instead gets no warning. (b) docs/RFC-undo-redo.md:57/75/89/114 documents the `<GanttProvider>` public API (`<GanttProvider historyDepth={N}>`, `useHistory()`, `<GanttProvider keyboardShortcuts={false}>`) that the createContext/Ctx.Provider change at README.md:106 and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:67 touches, and line 118 claims a pattern 'is already idiomatic SolidJS' — a claim that needs re-checking against 2.0. (c) docs/CONSTRAINTS.md (576 lines) and docs/SUBTASKS.md (268 lines) contain no Solid API references (verified by grep) and genuinely need nothing. The batch file list should be extended to (a) and (b).

EVERY TOOLING FILE THIS MIGRATION EDITS IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY QUALITY GATE. tsconfig.json:22 `include` omits config/vite/*.js, vitest.config.ts, eslint.config.mjs and server/**; package.json:30 (lint) and :33 (prettier-check) use the same four globs (src, tests, server, benchmarks/constraint) and omit the config files; .github/workflows/publish.yml runs only prettier-check + build. So a broken `@solidjs/vite-plugin` import, a mistyped plugin option, or a wrong jsxImportSource reaches `npm publish` unchallenged — and the audit's own recommendation to add typecheck+test to CI is worth nothing for these files until the include/lint globs are widened first. Fix the globs and the CI step together, in that order.

TWO EXTERNALIZED RUNTIMES, ZERO GLOBAL BUILDS, ONE UNRESOLVED PACKAGING DECISION. config/vite/solid.js:14 emits `['es','umd']`; L18 externalizes the runtimes; L20-23 maps them to globals; package.json:5-6 and the `exports.require` condition point at ganttss.umd.js; README has no install section. Neither solid-js@2.0.0-rc.6 nor @solidjs/web@2.0.0-rc.6 publishes an IIFE build (both dist trees are ESM+CJS only; unpkg points at ESM), so the UMD half of that chain has been decorative and is about to become twice as decorative. Decide once — drop `umd`, or add a separate self-contained bundle with `external: []` — and propagate to package.json main/exports and the README in the same commit.

SMA CROSS-CHECK CONFIRMED: I read the full sma-report.txt (200 lines). It names exactly two files, benchmarks/constraint/earlyTerminationBench.ts and benchmarks/profiler/instrumentation/memoTracker.js:136 (createMemo initial-value argument), plus src/components/Gantt.tsx:184 (split createEffect). NOT ONE in-scope file appears — no package.json, no vite/vitest/tsconfig/eslint config, no workflow, no markdown. The audit's claim of zero SMA overlap is accurate, which means 100% of this batch's coverage is human/agent-derived and nothing here has an automated cross-check behind it.
critic.summary:
I re-grepped every FACTS pattern across the 17 in-scope files, read the full sma-report.txt, and verified claims directly against the published tarballs (solid-js/@solidjs/web/@solidjs/signals 2.0.0-rc.6, @solidjs/vite-plugin next.35 AND next.38, @solid-primitives/raf 4.0.0-next.2). The audit is strong on mechanics — its dependency swap, external/globals re-keying, jsxImportSource change, and the serverTestPosture analysis all check out line-for-line against the plugin dist, and its line numbers are accurate. It has two blind spots.

The first is that its central vitest recommendation is unscoped. 'Delete environment:node, take the plugin's jsdom default' is right for the 11 reactive suites and wrong for tests/server/{routes,crud,adapter,schema}.test.ts, which drive better-sqlite3 and Hono via `app.fetch(new Request(...))` and which the audit never opens — it justifies jsdom with 'no test currently touches document/window', a grep that simply misses them. The plugin's own source says posture is per-vitest-project, so vitest 4 `test.projects` is the only shape that serves both, and the audit's fallback ('keep an explicit browser condition under environment:node') is worse than it looks: that branch also force-inlines the runtimes for a server build, so forcing browser back yields client reactivity + server codegen + no DOM, a hybrid upstream deliberately refuses to emit.

The second is a false-negative on Set-in-store. The audit surveyed taskStore.collapsedTasks (a signal-of-Set, correctly benign) and let that stand as the answer, missing ganttConfigStore.expandedTasks — declared inside GanttConfigState, created inside createStore, and mutated in place at three sites via `setState('expandedTasks', produce(set => set.add/delete(id)))`. That is a triple break (unproxied Set, removed produce, removed path setter) and the only silent one in the store layer.

Beyond those: @solid-primitives/raf is being bumped to a prerelease while left in `dependencies` even though nothing reachable from src/index.ts imports it; the UMD format plus two externalized runtimes is an unsatisfiable contract because neither package publishes a global build; `output: { interop: 'auto' }` in config/vite/solid.js sits at the config top level where Vite ignores it; and tsconfig include, lint globs, prettier globs and CI collectively give every file this migration edits zero static verification. On docs I add nine sites the audit passed over, the most consequential being docs/PERFORMANCE.md:421, where the documented untrack 'fix' only wraps the proxy lookup and leaves every `bar.x`/`bar.width` read tracked — a pattern that is already a no-op in 1.x and starts emitting STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED in 2.0. I also recommend @solidjs/vite-plugin next.38 over next.35 (matching @solidjs/compiler rc.6, and it adds the `mode !== 'test'` guards next.35 lacks) and note that AGENTS.md and docs/RFC-undo-redo.md carry in-scope guidance but were left off the batch list.

tracer.summary: Traced all ten requested chains plus three additional ones by opening every file in each path. The library splits cleanly into two populations. The per-frame drag loop is largely sound: within one rAF frame every pipeline reads before it writes (useBarDrag.ts:155-164, :183-199; taskLayerConstraints.ts:60-73), rAF frames are separate tasks so cross-frame reads see committed state, and the two write primitives that look dangerous are actually safe — batchMovePositions' produce callback reads state[id] inside the draft (taskStore.ts:161-172), and every selectionStore mutator uses a functional updater that rc.6 folds against the staged value (selectionStore.ts:40-69, exercised in a loop at useBoxSelect.ts:156). Do not "fix" those. What genuinely breaks clusters at four seams. First, the setup pipeline is write-then-read four times over: ganttDateStore.setupDates writes ganttStart/ganttEnd at :193-194 then generateDates reads them back at :202-203, ganttSetup.ts:66 then re-reads all five timeline values at :69-73 and :75-84, and ganttSetup.ts:101 writes resources then reads resourceIndexMap() on the very next line. That last one is worse than previously reported: an empty-but-non-null Map skips taskProcessor's internal fallback at :231-235, so every task gets effectiveRowIndex -1, isHidden true, y -1000 (taskProcessor.ts:243-262, :304) and useTaskVirtualization.ts:87 filters them all out — the first paint is a blank chart, not misplaced bars. Second, the gesture-commit boundary: useDrag.ts:161 runs the final onDragMove (which writes) and useDrag.ts:177 calls onDragEnd in the same synchronous stack, where useBarDrag.ts:271 reads getBarPosition back and useBarDrag.ts:281 reads a progress memo back. That single seam is the root of chains C, D and H, including DbDemo persisting drag deltas short by one frame with an error that compounds across drags (DbDemo.tsx:195-196 vs :239-242). Third, ganttConfigStore's expandedTasks is a raw Set mutated in place inside a store (:146, :172-203) — a total reactivity loss independent of deferral — compounded by committed-read guards at :186/:196 and by the count-only virtualization cache at useTaskVirtualization.ts:78 and TaskLayerMinimal.tsx:53, which rc.6's flush coalescing renders permanently stale. Fourth, taskStore's committed-read guards: updateBarPosition's `if (!tasks[id]) return` at :108 (which silently drops writes for tasks created earlier in the same turn), collapseAllTasks reading the task map at :234 before writing at :243, and removeTask's 1.x delete idiom at :134 that no longer removes the key. Two seed hazards are refuted or downgraded: the ArrowLayer/Arrow chain is demo-only (the shipped Gantt mounts no arrow layer — grep of Gantt.tsx, GanttContainer.tsx and TaskLayer.tsx finds no ArrowLayer usage; only demo/GanttPerfIsolate.tsx:2015 does), and the box-select/selection reads are correct in a real browser because click and mousedown are separate tasks, breaking only under synthetic-event drivers.
tracer.verdict: Roughly 80% mechanical edits, 20% genuine restructuring, and the restructuring is concentrated in two places rather than smeared across the drag pipeline. The drag/constraint machinery itself does NOT need rewriting: the per-frame loop already reads before it writes, constraintEngine.calculateCascadeUpdates carries its own pending-update overlay (:634-636, :645-647) so a single call is internally consistent, and successive rAF frames are separate tasks with a flush between. What needs real design work is (1) the setup pipeline — ganttSetup.ts plus ganttDateStore's setupDates/generateDates/changeViewMode/extendTimeline must be converted from write-then-read-back into compute-then-apply, with generateDates taking explicit (start, end, step, unit) parameters and the resource index map computed locally from the extracted array instead of round-tripped through the store; and (2) the gesture-commit boundary in useDrag.ts:161-177, where the final onDragMove's write is read back by onDragEnd, onResizeEnd and every downstream consumer in the same stack — thread the committed geometry out as a local or return value and chains C, D and H all close at once, including the DbDemo data-corruption path. Everything else is a one-liner or close to it: delete the committed-state guard at taskStore.ts:108 (the draft callback at :112-113 already checks correctly), change the re-entrancy guard at useDrag.ts:196 from dragState() to dragData (matching the pattern already used at :130 and :155), move expandedTasks to a replace-never-mutate signal, pass measured container dimensions as data rather than accessors in the GanttContainer handshake, move the isScrolling flag and timer out of the tracked compute at useGanttScroll.ts:78-90, give collapseAllTasks and resourceStore.collapseAll an explicit id-list parameter, fix removeTask to actually delete the key, and key the virtualization cache on a version counter instead of a task count. The highest-severity item to fix first is chain A, because it fails closed — a blank chart on first paint with no error and no warning — and the highest-consequence is chain H, because its stale read is persisted to a database rather than merely displayed.
